title: Add cold-start and weekly_scoped identity-change tests for the production path
description:
Split from parent bf-12wx4 (umbrella). Depends on Children 1-3. Closes the test-coverage gaps the parent's acceptance criteria demand.

PROBLEM: no existing test simulates a window CHANGING IDENTITY (the src/burn_rate.rs weekly_scoped tests at line ~2629 start each model-parametrized case from a fresh empty ema_state -- they never seed model A's samples and then assert model B gets a clean reset). And no test asserts the PRODUCTION cold-start behavior (cold window does not report 0.0 burn with high confidence).

SCOPE -- add tests that exercise the PRODUCTION path (governor.rs inline EMA + generate_window_forecast), NOT the test-only estimate_burn_rates:
1. COLD-START: a window with 0 prior samples reports a seeded (non-zero) base rate AND is flagged cold/uncertain via the Child-1 signal -- it does NOT report exactly 0.0 burn with high implied confidence.
2. IDENTITY CHANGE: seed weekly_scoped=Fable samples until calibrated, then rotate the scoped model to a different name mid-run and assert the slot resets: samples -> 0, signal -> cold, rate -> seeded base rate (NOT Fable's stale rate, NOT 0.0). This is the parent's headline acceptance test.
3. REGRESSION: a continuously-calibrated window's forecast is numerically unchanged by Children 1-3 (guard the "only the cold path changes" invariant).
4. (If practical) FIRST-STARTUP: a brand-new state (no persisted weekly_scoped_model, no samples) cold-starts flagged cold/uncertain, NOT as confident-empty.

ACCEPTANCE:
- All four behaviors asserted; the identity-change and cold-start tests FAIL if any of Children 1-3 are reverted (so they genuinely guard the fix).
- Full cargo test suite green.
- The identity-change test is the explicit verification of the parent's "simulate Fable -> other model" acceptance criterion.

title: OPS-GATED: lab checkout has origin=GitHub, not Forgejo; diverged commit history vs the canonical clone
description:
git remote -v on lab (host 100.81.129.38, path /home/coding/claude-governor) shows origin pointing at github.com/jedarden/claude-governor. Org-wide policy (this repo CLAUDE.md, Git Hosting section) is Forgejo (git.ardenone.com) as the source of truth with GitHub as a read-only server-side push mirror - client-side pushes should only ever target Forgejo.

A separate existing clone of this same repo has origin correctly pointing at git.ardenone.com, but sits at a different commit (a chore/seeder commit about default polish-queue push behavior) that shares no visible recent history with lab HEAD (a long chain of docs commits documenting test-verification results and a Children 1-3 revert-then-restore cycle, dated 2026-07-27).

If lab has been pushing directly to GitHub, Forgejo does not have those commits, and Forgejo server-side push mirror (Forgejo to GitHub) could conflict with or silently overwrite lab independent GitHub history on its next sync, or vice versa - either direction risks losing one side commits.

This needs a human to: confirm which line of commits is meant to be canonical, reconcile via a merge commit (never force-push, per standing policy), and repoint lab origin at Forgejo once reconciled. Flagging as a current-state finding for a human decision - git remote and history surgery is out of scope for this audit.

title: Document Pluck query results
burn_rate.rs: replace zero-assumption cold-start default with an estimated base rate
description:
Depends on bf-oeotj (dynamic weekly_scoped generalization).

poller.rs's window_or_default() returns (0.0 utilization, \"\", 168.0 hours_remaining) for any window the API reports as null/absent. That is a reasonable PARSE-time default (do not change it there -- it correctly means \"nothing to report\"), but burn_rate.rs currently carries that 0.0 straight through into its own utilization/burn-rate model for a window that has NO samples yet -- effectively assuming zero usage / infinite headroom for anything new.

This is a real risk, flagged by the user during triage (not yet observed causing harm, but structurally live): every time the model named by weekly_scoped changes (Anthropic rotates which model gets a scoped weekly cap -- it was presumably sonnet once, is Fable now, could be a third model later), or the very first time cgov starts up, that window cold-starts at an ASSUMED 0% utilization with full confidence, rather than an honest \"we don't know yet.\" A governor that treats \"no data\" as \"definitely empty\" can over-scale a subscription pool right before the window's TRUE usage (inherited from whatever was happening before cgov started tracking it, or from other non-cgov usage on the same account) turns out to be much higher, blowing through the real limit with no warning.

Fix: when a window (any of the three, but this matters most for the dynamic scoped-weekly slot since it can change identity) has fewer than N samples (pick a reasonable minimum, e.g. 3, matching whatever cadence makes a real EMA meaningful) or has never been observed non-null before, seed its assumed burn rate from a conservative BASE RATE rather than 0. Reasonable base-rate sources to consider (pick one, document why):
  - the account's own weekly_all (pooled, always-present) EMA pct/hr as a proxy, since a model-scoped window is a subset of overall usage and inherits similar burn dynamics;
  - a configurable conservative floor (e.g. assume the window is already at some non-trivial % used until proven otherwise) set in governor.yaml;
  - the actual API-reported current .percent value taken at face value for utilization (this IS already correct and is NOT the bug -- the bug is specifically the burn RATE / trend extrapolation defaulting to 0 change-per-hour, not the instantaneous percent).

Acceptance:
- A fresh/cold window (0 prior samples) does not report a burn rate of exactly 0.0 with high implied confidence; it reports an estimated rate with a marked-uncertain/wide-margin flag, OR degrades gracefully to \"hold at current worker count until N samples accumulate\" -- pick one, document the choice in a code comment and in this bead's closing note.
- Existing calibrated (non-cold) windows' behavior is unchanged -- this only affects the cold-start/no-data path.
- Test: simulate the scoped-weekly model changing identity mid-run (e.g. Fable -> some other model) and confirm the newly-appearing window does not silently claim 0% utilization / infinite headroom for its first cycle.

title: config/claude-governor.service still ships MemoryMax=512M — the exact value that caused the July 2026 OOM crash-loop
description:
On 2026-07-22 claude-governor.service repeatedly OOM-killed on lab (journalctl: 9 kills between 14:26-15:14, each at 512M memory peak) — a hardcoded MemoryMax=512M crash-looping the daemon. The live deployed unit (~/.config/systemd/user/claude-governor.service on lab) was subsequently hand-patched to MemoryMax=6G out of band (confirmed via systemctl --user cat claude-governor: stable running 1+ week at 6G, peak RSS seen ~3.7G) — but this fix was never backported into the repo.

config/claude-governor.service (Resource limits section) and docs/plan/plan.md Phase 6.2 (~line 1793, the embedded systemd unit example) BOTH still hardcode MemoryMax=512M.

Because cgov init/cgov enable install this file via include_str!("../config/claude-governor.service") (src/main.rs, run_enable/install logic) and SKIP writing when the target unit already exists (only overwritten with --force), the current lab host is accidentally safe. But: cgov enable --force, a fresh install (new host, disaster recovery, wiped ~/.config), or anyone following the plan doc verbatim will reintroduce the exact 512M limit that caused the crash loop.

Related: the live unit's Documentation= URL still points at the wrong GitHub org (anthropics instead of jedarden) — already fixed in the repo per bf-2sxdp (closed) but never redeployed to the live unit, for the identical underlying reason: no reconciliation path between repo config and already-installed systemd units.

Acceptance criteria:
- config/claude-governor.service and the Phase 6.2 example in docs/plan/plan.md both set a safe MemoryMax (the field-proven 6G, or a smaller but comfortably-validated value based on measured daemon RSS)
- A comment in config/claude-governor.service and/or plan.md records why 512M was unsafe (cite the 2026-07-22 OOM crash-loop)
- Consider whether cgov doctor or cgov enable should warn (not silently skip) when an existing installed unit's MemoryMax is lower than the shipped default, so future safe-limit corrections actually propagate instead of silently drifting forever
- Not a live-redeploy task: only the repo-tracked config/plan need to change here; redeploying the corrected unit to any live host is a separate, human-supervised step

title: Token collector crash-loops forever on corrupt collector-cursors.json with zero recovery
description:
Evidence (live, currently active): the deployed claude-token-collector.service on this lab host has been failing EVERY collection pass since 2026-07-12 14:56 (file mtime) with the identical error repeating every ~2 min: "[collector] collection pass failed: Failed to load cursors: JSON error: expected comma or closing-brace at line 9576 column 105". Confirmed via: systemctl --user status claude-token-collector.service (Active: running the whole time -- the service never crashes, it just silently fails every cycle, so it LOOKS healthy while being functionally dead). The governor alert manager independently confirms it: governor.log shows "[alert] firing [WARNING] collector_offline: Token collector offline: last update 9873 minutes ago" (~6.9 days). Root cause located at ~/.needle/state/collector-cursors.json line ~9576: a malformed entry where two cursor byte-offset values are glued together with no separating key (e.g. an entry like PATH: 5841: 98899, -- a numeric value immediately followed by a colon and another value with no intervening quoted key), indicating a corrupted write. Plan Component 2 documents CursorStore save() as writing atomically via tmp-file-plus-rename (src/collector.rs CursorStore::save(), ~line 179, confirms this exists), but the tmp path is a FIXED path (path.with_extension(tmp)) -- if two collector-writing processes or passes ever overlap (e.g. a manual one-shot collection run racing the long-running daemon, or two overlapping slow passes), concurrent file-create calls on the same fixed tmp path truncate each other mid-write, producing exactly this kind of interleaved corruption even though the final rename step is atomic. The real bug: CursorStore load() (src/collector.rs ~line 167-176) has NO corruption recovery -- a serde_json parse error propagates straight up through run_collection_pass() via the message Failed to load cursors, and aborts the entire pass, forever, with no backoff, no quarantine, no reset. Contrast with the plan (docs/plan/plan.md Component 2, Fast-query SQLite mirror note): JSONL is authoritative, DB rebuilt on corruption -- there is no equivalent self-healing story for collector-cursors.json, and the existing shrinkage-guard in read_new_lines (which handles an individual tracked files cursor shrinking) does not cover the cursor STORE FILE ITSELF being corrupt.

Acceptance criteria:
1. In CursorStore load() (src/collector.rs), on a JSON parse error: back up the corrupt file (e.g. rename to path plus .corrupt- plus unix-timestamp), log a WARN with the parse error and the backup path, and return an empty default cursor map instead of propagating the error. This matches the existing shrinkage-guard philosophy of reset-and-rescan rather than crash-forever. Note the tradeoff in a code comment: resetting to empty means every known JSONL file will be re-read from byte 0 on the next pass, which will inflate that one intervals token deltas once (already-collected data gets re-counted one time) -- do not attempt full byte-exact recovery, that is out of scope.
2. Fix the concurrency hazard in CursorStore save(): use a unique tmp filename per writer (e.g. include the process id and/or a random suffix in the tmp path) so two concurrent save() calls cannot truncate or interleave each other -- a manual one-shot collection command invoked while the daemon collector is also running is a realistic trigger and should not corrupt shared state.
3. Add unit tests: (a) load() on a file with malformed JSON returns Ok(default) and creates a corrupt-marker backup rather than erroring; (b) load() on a valid file still works normally; (c) concurrent save() calls (simulate via two CursorStore instances writing to the same path) do not produce interleaved or corrupt output.
4. cargo build --release and cargo test --release stay green.
5. Optional but recommended for validation: on this lab host, after the fix ships and is installed, the currently-corrupt ~/.needle/state/collector-cursors.json can be renamed aside as a backup and the token-collector service restarted to confirm it recovers and starts writing fresh records again. This is a local, reversible, non-secret file on the dev host, not a K8s or GitOps-managed resource.

Safety note: primary worker-scaling safety is NOT compromised by this outage -- the cutoff-risk percentage forecast is computed from direct poller API snapshots (src/governor.rs, roughly lines 2870-2920), decoupled from the token collector by design per the plan (the governor reads from its output but does not depend on it being active to function). The impact is limited to stale and frozen dollar-denominated burn rate and cache-efficiency metrics -- still worth fixing, but not an emergency-brake-level issue.

title: Implement ADR-001: split cgov daemon into _observe/_act processes (Status: Proposed, not implemented)
description:
docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 (dated 2026-07-20, ~line 2066) documents a decision to split cgov _daemon into two independently-supervised processes: cgov _observe (poll, burn-rate EMA, capacity-forecast, confidence-cone, calibrator, safe-mode; writes governor-state.json; never acts) and cgov _act (reads that state, only performs apply_scaling and check_alerts/fire_alert). Motivation: today, the only way to stop untrusted scaling/alerting is to kill the whole daemon, which also stops the harmless Observe half - starving the calibrator of the very data needed to decide when re-enabling Act is safe. ADR-001 documents this happened at least twice historically (docs/notes/bf-48qtz.md, then regression by 2026-06-28).

ADR-001 Status is still Proposed. No code in src/governor.rs or src/main.rs implements the split (single _daemon subcommand remains), no new systemd unit files exist in config/, and no bead in this workspace tracks the implementation - the ADR own Follow-up section explicitly scoped out only the narrower problems found alongside it (stale pricing table, already fixed; wrong default alert-bead command, filed separately; duplicate systemd units, already fixed per bf-4vf4q closed; alert-bead spam, tracked via docs-878a and auto_bead), noting the full split itself should be filed as its own bead once someone picks the ADR up. Nobody has yet.

Acceptance criteria, per ADR-001 Decision section:
- New cgov _observe and cgov _act hidden subcommands extracted from the current _daemon loop in src/governor.rs
- State file ownership split as specified in the ADR: observe owns the usage, forecast, burn rate, schedule, calibration, safe mode and FP telemetry fields; act owns worker targets, alert cooldowns, and appends to the alert list
- New observe and act systemd unit files added under config/; cgov enable, disable and stop updated to accept a target argument of observe, act, or all (default all)
- cgov doctor distinguishes a stopped observe process (hard fail) from an intentionally paused act process (warn, not fail)
- Deploying and cutting over the new units on any live host (e.g. lab) is an explicit, separate, human-supervised follow-up step once the code lands, not part of this bead acceptance

title: Implement SQLite UPDATE logic for i/f row annotation
description:
Add the core SQLite annotation logic in src/db.rs or a new db module: a function that takes window deltas (p5h, p7d, p7ds) for a specific interval and performs UPDATE queries on the token-history.db mirror.

The function must:
1. Accept interval bounds (start/end timestamps) and the three delta values
2. For each i row in the interval: UPDATE p5h/p7d/p7ds to the apportioned value (weighted by that row's total_usd relative to sum of all i rows' total_usd in the interval)
3. For the f row in the interval: UPDATE p5h/p7d/p7ds to the full (unapportioned) delta values
4. Use a transaction to ensure atomic updates

Formula: row_p7ds = delta * (row_total_usd / sum_total_usd)

Add unit tests using an in-memory SQLite database with synthetic i and f rows to verify:
- Correct apportioning across 2+ i rows
- f row gets full deltas
- Transaction rolls back on error

Acceptance criteria:

title: Seed cold-start windows from a conservative base rate in the production governor path
description:
Split from parent bf-12wx4 (umbrella). Depends on Child 1's cold-start signal. THIS IS THE CORE FIX the parent describes.

PROBLEM: a window with fewer than MIN_SAMPLES_FOR_EMA (=3, src/burn_rate.rs:149) samples currently reports a burn rate that effectively defaults toward 0 change-per-hour, i.e. "infinite headroom," with no uncertainty marker. A governor that treats "no data" as "definitely empty" can over-scale right before true usage turns out to be much higher.

CRITICAL CONTEXT (from bf-12wx4 investigation): the cold-start seeding logic at src/burn_rate.rs:1390-1461 is inside estimate_burn_rates, which is DEAD CODE IN PRODUCTION (test-only -- verify the call sites; the governor never calls it). The real per-window EMA is updated INLINE at src/governor.rs:4023-4141 and the forecast is built by generate_window_forecast. This child MUST land in the production path (governor.rs inline + generate_window_forecast), NOT only in the test-only function -- otherwise it "passes" without fixing anything.

SCOPE:
- When a window is cold (< MIN_SAMPLES_FOR_EMA samples, e.g. first startup or a slot just reset to 0 samples by Child 3), seed its EFFECTIVE burn rate from a conservative BASE RATE rather than 0.0.
- BASE-RATE SOURCE (pick THIS one, document why in a code comment AND in the closing note): the per-agent baseline_burn_rate already in config (AgentConfig.baseline_burn_rate, src/config.rs:80-93; accessor baseline_burn_rate_or_default, default 1.5 pct/worker/hr). Rationale: already present, already conservative, already per-agent-configurable, and needs no new coupling. The parent bead also offered weekly_all EMA-as-proxy or a new governor.yaml floor; the per-agent baseline is the smallest correct choice. If investigation shows weekly_all proxy is materially better, pick it instead but document the trade-off.
- Mark every cold-seeded estimate via the Child-1 signal (ColdStart / InsufficientSamples) AND keep the cone wide (uncertain) so the governor sees "estimated, not measured."
- Calibrated windows (>= MIN_SAMPLES_FOR_EMA) are UNCHANGED -- this child only affects the cold/no-data path.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A cold window (0 prior samples) does NOT report a burn rate of exactly 0.0 with high implied confidence; it reports the seeded base rate, flagged cold/uncertain via the Child-1 signal.
- Calibrated windows' forecasts are numerically unchanged (regression-protect with existing forecast tests).
- The fix is in the PRODUCTION path (governor.rs inline / generate_window_forecast), not only in the test-only estimate_burn_rates.
- A code comment documents the base-rate choice; the closing note restates it.

title: Implement stale-heartbeat handling per plan: 60s threshold, tmux verification, orphan file removal
description:
Plan section: Component 6 (Worker Manager), 'Heartbeat file format' subsection in docs/plan/plan.md. Spec: 'Heartbeat files older than 60 seconds are treated as stale — the worker may have crashed without cleanup. Stale heartbeats are verified against tmux list-sessions before any action is taken; if the tmux session no longer exists, the heartbeat file is removed.'

Current state (static review): src/worker.rs read_heartbeats() (~line 401) parses all heartbeat JSON files with NO staleness check on the heartbeat timestamp, and nothing anywhere removes orphaned heartbeat files. Consequences:
- After a worker crashes without cleanup, its heartbeat file persists forever; WorkerCount.consistent (count_workers, ~line 118) stays false permanently and heartbeat_count is inflated.
- find_workers_to_stop() (~line 373) can select a dead worker's session (it sorts old heartbeats first as 'may be dead'), causing scale-down cycles to send SIGINT/kill to nonexistent tmux sessions and burn the scale-down budget on ghosts.
Note: the governor already uses tmux_count as the authoritative current count (src/governor.rs ~line 1475), so scaling targets are correct — the gap is stale-file hygiene and shutdown-selection correctness, exactly what the plan specifies.

Implement in src/worker.rs:
1. Add a staleness threshold (60s, ideally a named const) comparing the heartbeat's updated_at/timestamp field to now.
2. When a heartbeat is stale, verify against tmux list-sessions: if the session no longer exists, delete the heartbeat file (log at info level); if the session exists, treat status as executing (never kill based on a stale idle status).
3. Exclude removed/orphaned heartbeats from heartbeat_count and from find_workers_to_stop candidates.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests: (a) stale heartbeat + dead session => file removed and excluded from counts; (b) stale heartbeat + live session => retained but never selected as idle for shutdown; (c) fresh heartbeat behavior unchanged
- count_workers().consistent recovers to true after a crashed worker's heartbeat is cleaned up
- No behavior change for fresh (<60s) heartbeats; cargo test passes

title: Epic: adapt usage-window model to the real dynamic-scoped-weekly API (not hardcoded sonnet)
description:
cgov currently assumes the account's per-model weekly cap is always named \"sonnet\" (WINDOWS const hardcodes [five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_sonnet] in burn_rate.rs). Confirmed live 2026-07-26/27 against the real /api/oauth/usage payload that this assumption is wrong for the current account state:

  seven_day_sonnet: null   (does not exist)
  seven_day_opus:   null   (does not exist)
  limits: [
    {kind: session,       percent: 2},
    {kind: weekly_all,    percent: 69},
    {kind: weekly_scoped, percent: 79, scope.model.display_name: \"Fable\"}
  ]

The API has moved to (or this account only ever had) a generic limits[] array where the model-scoped weekly cap is DYNAMIC -- whichever model currently has one, named via scope.model.display_name. Right now that's Fable, not sonnet. Two compounding bugs result:

1. cgov never reads limits[]/weekly_scoped at all -- it is blind to the REAL tightest constraint on the account (Fable, 79% used / 21% remaining).
2. burn_rate.rs's binding-window selection treats the permanently-null seven_day_sonnet as \"insufficient data, hold at current worker count\" -- logged repeatedly as \"binding window seven_day_sonnet: insufficient burn rate data, will hold at current worker count\" / \"target workers: 0\" -- forever, since that window can never populate for this account. This is what silently held the polish-opus pool (subscription-billed Opus generator, min0/max4) at 0 workers indefinitely, even though real headroom (weekly_all 31% remaining, session 98% remaining) was fine.

Cross-checked against usage-statusline.sh (~/.claude/usage-statusline.sh on the Hetzner box), which reads limits[] directly by kind and is unaffected by this -- proof the real API shape is parseable this way today.

Scope: generalize the \"third window\" concept from a fixed sonnet identity to whatever limits[] currently reports as weekly_scoped, across poller.rs / state.rs / burn_rate.rs / governor.rs, plus fix cold-start defaulting and binding-window candidacy for windows with no data. See child beads. This bead closes when all children are closed and a redeploy on lab confirms the governor's binding-window log reflects reality (Fable/weekly_all, not a phantom sonnet stall).

title: Reset weekly_scoped slot samples when the scoped model identity changes
description:
Split from parent bf-12wx4 (umbrella). Depends on Child 1 (signal) and Child 2 (the cold-seeding path this feeds into).

PROBLEM: weekly_scoped state is keyed by SLOT, not by model (see the persisted comment at src/state.rs:49-56: "the binding key stays the generic weekly_scoped"). When Anthropic rotates which model carries the scoped weekly cap (Sonnet -> Fable -> a third model), NO new window record appears -- the same weekly_scoped slot reuses the PREVIOUS model's EMA samples (WindowPctDeltas.weekly_scoped src/state.rs:133-147, PrevUsageSnapshot.weekly_scoped_pct src/state.rs:155-172, fleet_pct_ema_samples src/state.rs:468). Stale data from model A is then treated as authoritative for model B -- a different flavor of the cold-start bug (stale-as-authoritative rather than zero-as-empty).

ALSO: a leftover Sonnet hard-coding in the production path reads the new weekly_scoped value from state.usage.sonnet_pct (src/governor.rs:4044) instead of the model-agnostic limits[]-derived value -- fix this so the rotated model's REAL pct feeds the EMA.

SCOPE:
- Detect when the persisted weekly_scoped_model (src/state.rs:57) differs from the newly-resolved model name (UsageData::scoped_weekly / weekly_scoped_display_label, src/poller.rs:244-261 and src/state.rs:81-83). On change: RESET the weekly_scoped slot's samples to 0 (cold) so it flows into Child 2's base-rate seeding, and clear PrevUsageSnapshot.weekly_scoped_pct so the first new-model interval is not computed against the old model's snapshot. Then update the persisted weekly_scoped_model to the new name.
- Fix src/governor.rs:4044 to read the new weekly_scoped pct from the model-agnostic source, NOT sonnet_pct.
- Persisted fields STAY slot-keyed (do NOT re-key by model in this child -- that is a larger change the parent explicitly deferred; a reset-on-identity-change achieves the safety goal with the small option).

ACCEPTANCE:
- Simulate weekly_scoped identity changing Fable -> other mid-run: the slot's samples reset to 0, the window is flagged cold (Child-1 signal) and seeded from base rate (Child 2) for its first cycle -- it does NOT silently carry Fable's samples as authoritative, and does NOT claim 0% / infinite headroom.
- src/governor.rs:4044 no longer references sonnet_pct for weekly_scoped.
- Calibrated non-rotating windows unchanged; cargo test passes.

notes:
# Bug Summary: weekly_scoped Documentation Incorrectly States "Sonnet Only"

## Issue Description
The codebase contains documentation that incorrectly states `weekly_scoped` fields are "Sonnet only". In reality, these fields are **model-agnostic** and can be scoped to ANY model (Fable, Opus, Sonnet, etc.) depending on which model carries the scoped cap this period.

## Root Cause
The original implementation used a hardcoded `sonnet_pct` field, but the codebase was updated to use a model-agnostic design with:
- `UsageState.weekly_scoped_model`: Tracks which model (Fable, Opus, Sonnet, etc.) is active
- `UsageState.weekly_scoped_pct`: Model-agnostic utilization percentage
- Legacy `sonnet_pct` field: Kept for backward compatibility only (deprecated)

## Affected Lines in governor.rs
1. **Line 1454** - `make_window_pct_snapshot` documentation
2. **Line 1495** - `make_usage_snapshot` documentation  
3. **Line 1539** - `make_usage_snapshot_with_time` documentation
4. **Line 5519** - `tests::make_usage_snapshot` documentation
5. **Line 7632** - `MockPoller::with_utilization` documentation
6. **Line 7709** - `default_usage_data` documentation

## What Was Done
Bead bf-v9vqpj added inline code comments (commit e1c8b3c) at each location documenting:
- The bug: Documentation incorrectly states "Sonnet only"
- The fix: `weekly_scoped` is MODEL-AGNOSTIC
- Reference: Points to `state.rs UsageState.weekly_scoped_model` and `weekly_scoped_pct` fields

## Next Steps for the Fix
1. Update all 6 documentation lines to replace "Sonnet only" with "model-agnostic (Fable, Opus, Sonnet, etc.)"
2. Update any related tests or documentation that reference the old behavior
3. Verify the fix with full test suite (already validated in bf-2uqbeo)

## References
- state.rs lines 53-77: Model-agnostic weekly_scoped implementation

title: Implement governor-side p5h/p7d/p7ds annotation of collector records (unblocks empirical promotion validation)
description:
Plan sections: Component 2 (Token Collector — 'p5h, p7d, p7ds are null at write time. The governor annotates them in the SQLite mirror by apportioning each window's observed percentage delta across concurrent sessions, weighted by total-usd') and Phase 1b step 3 (window_pct_deltas annotation) in docs/plan/plan.md.

Current state (static review): the annotation step was never implemented. src/collector.rs writes p5h/p7d/p7ds as null on both i and f records; a comment in src/governor.rs (~line 1503) confirms: 'The fleet record's p5h/p7d/p7ds fields are always null (the collector writes them null and never fills them in)'. The governor works around this for burn-rate EMA by diffing consecutive API poll snapshots, so scaling works — but downstream features that read the annotated columns are permanently dead:
1. compute_empirical_promo_ratio() in src/burn_rate.rs (~line 498) queries i records WHERE p7ds IS NOT NULL AND p7ds > 0 — always returns no rows, so validate_promotion_from_db() always fails with 'no data found in token-history DB' and empirical promotion validation can never succeed (the conservative 1.0 multiplier fallback would be used through an entire real promotion).
2. The usd-per-pct-7ds column and the promo_check / instance_compare SQLite views in src/db.rs compute NULL forever.

Implement:
1. In the governor cycle (src/governor.rs), after each poll: take the per-window pct delta between consecutive API snapshots for the interval matching the latest collector records, and UPDATE the i rows for that interval in the SQLite mirror (~/.needle/state/token-history.db), apportioning each window's delta across concurrent sessions weighted by each row's total_usd. Fill the f row for the interval with the full (unapportioned) deltas.
2. Guard conditions per plan Component 5: skip when the interval spans a window reset, when elapsed < 2 min, or when worker count changed mid-interval.
3. Keep JSONL authoritative-but-null semantics (annotation lives in the DB mirror, per plan) — do not rewrite JSONL lines.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit test: given 2 synthetic i rows with total_usd 0.10 and 0.30 and a window delta of 0.8, annotation writes p7ds 0.2 and 0.6 respectively; f row gets 0.8
- Unit test: compute_empirical_promo_ratio() returns Some(...) after annotation of >=10 peak and >=10 off-peak synthetic intervals
- instance_compare and promo_check views return non-NULL usd_per_pct_7ds for annotated intervals
- cargo test passes; no changes to scaling behavior when annotation data is absent (existing API-delta EMA path untouched)

title: Collector-offline three-tier fallback to baseline_burn_rate is not implemented despite bead docs-y5p claiming completion
description:
Evidence: docs/plan/plan.md Component 5 (Adaptive Burn Rate Estimator), Token collector offline graceful degradation section, specifies a three-tier fallback keyed on collector data staleness: under 10 minutes = use normally; 10-30 minutes = use last EMA values plus a WARN log; over 30 minutes = fall back to baseline_burn_rate from governor.yaml and create a HUMAN alert bead. The Configuration File section of the plan documents a per-agent baseline_burn_rate field (e.g. baseline_burn_rate: 1.2 percent per worker per hour) intended as that fallback value. A bead (docs-y5p, P3: Token collector offline graceful degradation) was already closed claiming this was implemented, but the implementation does not match: grep -rn baseline_burn_rate src/ config/governor.yaml returns zero matches anywhere in the codebase -- there is no such config field. What exists instead in src/burn_rate.rs is a DIFFERENT, hardcoded mechanism: BaselineBurnRates::default() returns fixed Rust constants (1.5 percent per worker per hour, 5 dollars per worker per hour) used only for the cold-start case (fewer than 3 EMA samples accumulated yet, per effective_burn_rate()) -- this is unrelated to collector staleness and is never sourced from governor.yaml. Separately, src/alerts.rs (~line 727-740) does fire a CollectorOffline WARNING alert at exactly the 30-minute threshold (comment there even says "matching the governors fallback-to-baseline staleness tier"), but firing an alert is not the same as the burn-rate estimator actually reverting to a baseline -- grep -rn collector_data_age src/ (the function name literally specified in docs-y5p acceptance criteria) returns zero matches, confirming that function was never written. Live confirmation on this lab deployment: the token collector has been offline since 2026-07-12 (see related bead about the collector-cursors.json corruption bug); governor.log shows the CollectorOffline alert correctly firing at the 30-minute mark and beyond, but state.last_fleet_aggregate (and derivatives like sonnet_p75_usd_hr used for dollar-denominated forecasts and cache-efficiency stats) has simply stayed frozen at its last-known value for over a week instead of reverting to any baseline -- there is no code path that would make it do otherwise.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Add a baseline_burn_rate config field to the per-agent config struct in src/config.rs (pct_per_worker_per_hour and dollars_per_worker_per_hour, mirroring the existing plan-documented schema), with the current hardcoded BaselineBurnRates::default() values (1.5, 5.0) as the struct-level Default so behavior is unchanged for configs that do not set it explicitly.
2. Wire BaselineBurnRates construction in src/burn_rate.rs to read from the loaded agent config instead of always calling BaselineBurnRates::default().
3. Add a collector_data_age-style staleness check (age of state.last_fleet_aggregate.t1 relative to now) that, when it exceeds 30 minutes, causes dollar-denominated burn-rate and forecast fields to revert to the configured baseline rather than continuing to use a frozen stale EMA value indefinitely. Follow the plans three tiers precisely: under 10 min normal, 10-30 min keep last EMA plus WARN log, over 30 min revert to baseline.
4. Add unit tests mirroring docs-y5p original testing requirements: fresh data under 10 min behaves normally; stale data at 15 min logs a warning and keeps last EMA; very stale data at 45 min falls back to the configured baseline; recovery after a stale period restores EMA-based rates within one interval.
5. cargo build --release and cargo test --release stay green.

Safety note: this does not affect primary worker-scaling safety, which runs on the separately-computed percentage-based EMA from direct poller snapshots and is unaffected by collector staleness. This gap only affects dollar-denominated and cache-efficiency reporting accuracy during collector outages.

title: state.rs: track per-window consecutive-absence count, null-tolerant and persisted
description:

Add a per-window consecutive-absence counter to state (state.rs) for each pooled window (five_hour, seven_day, and the dynamic weekly_scoped slot). Follow the existing null-tolerant deserialize conventions in state.rs (per CLAUDE.md section 8: an Inf serializes to null and must round-trip; the daemon must not discard calibration each cycle). The counter:
- Increments by 1 on a poll that reports the window null/absent (poller.rs window_or_default semantics; scoped_weekly() returns None for weekly_scoped).
- Resets to 0 the moment a window reports real data.
- Persists across cycles (the whole point is detecting absence over N consecutive polls, so it must survive a reconcile/restart).

Acceptance:
- New persisted, null-tolerant state field(s) for per-window consecutive-absence counts; round-trips through serialize/deserialize.
- Unit test: 3 consecutive absent polls for weekly_scoped yields counter == 3; a single present poll resets it to 0.
- Existing calibrated-window behavior unchanged; full suite green.

title: governor.rs: exclude structurally-inactive windows from binding-window candidacy (dont perpetually hold at 0 waiting for data that cannot arrive)
description:
Depends on bf-oeotj (dynamic weekly_scoped generalization). Related but independent of bf-12wx4 (base-rate cold-start) -- that bead fixes WHAT VALUE to assume when data is sparse; this bead fixes WHETHER a window should be considered a binding candidate at all when it has no realistic path to ever having data.

Observed live 2026-07-26/27: governor.rs logged, every 5-minute cycle, indefinitely:
  \"binding window seven_day_sonnet: insufficient burn rate data, will hold at current worker count\"
  \"target workers: 0\"
even though the OTHER two windows (five_hour, seven_day) had plenty of headroom and plenty of samples. The account structurally has no seven_day_sonnet limit (API returns null every single poll, confirmed over multiple consecutive cycles) -- this is not a transient warm-up state, it will NEVER resolve on its own. Once bf-oeotj lands, the equivalent failure mode can still occur for a generalized weekly_scoped window during any period where the API reports no active model-scoped cap at all (scoped_weekly() returns None) -- so this needs its own explicit handling, not just \"fixed by renaming.\"

Fix: a window should be excluded from binding-window candidacy (not merely deprioritized) when EITHER:
  - it is Option::None / absent from the API response across some minimum number of consecutive polls (distinguish one-off transient null from a settled absent state), OR
  - is_active == false is reported explicitly by the API for that limit entry (if that field is populated meaningfully -- check real payloads for this).
An excluded window contributes no ceiling to safe_worker_count and is never logged as \"BINDING\" -- the binding window becomes whichever REMAINING window is actually tightest.

Acceptance:
- Fixture: weekly_scoped absent across 3+ consecutive polls -> excluded from binding candidacy; the actual binding window becomes seven_day or five_hour (whichever is tighter), target_workers reflects real headroom, not 0.
- Fixture: weekly_scoped present with real data -> included and can legitimately become binding as before.
- No change to behavior for five_hour/seven_day (both are always-present pooled windows for every account state seen so far; this exclusion path is specifically for the dynamic scoped-weekly slot, though write it generically enough to apply to any window in case that changes too).

Add the collector_data_age staleness check in src/burn_rate.rs that implements the three-tier fallback specified in the plan.

close_reason:
Fixed false positive sonnet_cutoff_risk alert

The alert was firing even when margin_hrs was positive (safe). This was caused by missing validation of the margin_hrs field in the alert condition.

Per burn_rate.rs formula:
- margin_hrs = predicted_exhaustion_hours - hours_remaining
- Positive margin_hrs = safe (exhaustion after reset)
- Negative margin_hrs = risky (exhaustion before reset)

The fix adds a check for margin_hrs < 0.0 in both sonnet_cutoff_risk and session_cutoff_risk alert functions to prevent false positives from corrupted state or sign convention mismatches between modules.

Fix commit: 26c399d
Regression tests added to prevent recurrence.

description:
## WindowRecord Struct and Forecast Computation

Implement the WindowRecord struct and the forecast computation for all three windows.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add WindowRecord and forecast logic

### What to Implement
- `pub struct WindowRecord` with all schema fields:
  - `r: String` (always "w"), `ts: DateTime<Utc>`, `win: String` (window name: "five_hour", "seven_day", "seven_day_sonnet")
  - `pk: bool`, `ceil: f64` (target ceiling from config, e.g. 90.0)
  - `snap: f64` (raw platform utilization %), `reset: DateTime<Utc>` (window reset time)
  - `delta: f64` (pct change this interval), `remain: f64` (`ceil - snap`, NOT `100 - snap`)
  - `hrs_left: f64` (hours until reset), `fleet_pct_hr: f64` (fleet burn rate as pct/hr)
  - `exh_hrs: f64` (`remain / fleet_pct_hr`), `cutoff_risk: u8` (1 if `exh_hrs < hrs_left`)
  - `margin_hrs: f64` (`hrs_left - exh_hrs`)
  - `bind: u8` (1 if most constrained), `safe_w: Option<u32>` (only on binding window)
- `pub fn compute_window_forecast(win: &str, snap: f64, ceil: f64, reset: DateTime<Utc>, now: DateTime<Utc>, fleet_pct_hr: f64, pk: bool) -> WindowRecord`:
  - Compute all derived fields: remain, hrs_left, exh_hrs, cutoff_risk, margin_hrs
  - Leave bind=0 and safe_w=None (set by find_binding_window)

### Test Command
```bash
cargo test --lib collector::tests::window_forecast 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: ceil=90, snap=36 -> remain=54 (NOT 64)
- Unit test: hrs_left computed correctly from reset-now
- Unit test: exh_hrs = remain / fleet_pct_hr with known values
- Unit test: cutoff_risk=1 when exh_hrs < hrs_left
- Unit test: cutoff_risk=0 when exh_hrs > hrs_left
- Unit test: margin_hrs = hrs_left - exh_hrs (can be negative)
- Serialization: WindowRecord serializes with correct field names

title: P7: Cross-window capacity optimization
description:
## Task: Cross-Window Capacity Optimization

Optimize worker count across all three windows simultaneously using marginal cost weighting.

### What to Implement
- In `src/burn_rate.rs` (extend):
  - `window_cost(window: &WindowForecast) -> f64`:
    - scarcity = (1.0 / remaining_pct) * hrs_left
    - Short-horizon capacity is cheap; long-horizon is expensive
  - `composite_risk(n_workers, windows, burn_rate) -> f64`:
    - For each window: compute exhaust_hrs at N workers
    - If exhaust_hrs < hrs_left: risk += window_cost * (hrs_left - exhaust_hrs)
    - Sum across all windows
  - `optimal_workers(windows, burn_rate, max_workers, cost_threshold) -> u32`:
    - Max N where composite_risk(N) < cost_threshold
    - cost_threshold=0.0 (default) = never breach any window (equivalent to binding-window)
    - cost_threshold > 0 allows breaching cheap short-horizon windows
  - State schema extension:
    - `cross_window_optimal` field when enabled
    - Falls back to binding-window formula when disabled or in safe mode
  - Configurable via `cross_window.enabled` and `cross_window.cost_threshold`

### Files
- `src/burn_rate.rs` (extend)
- `src/governor.rs` (use composite risk when enabled)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: window_cost — short horizon cheap, long horizon expensive
- Unit test: composite_risk — 5h near-reset with ample 7d allows more workers
- Unit test: cost_threshold=0 behaves identically to binding-window approach
- Unit test: cost_threshold>0 allows more workers when only cheap windows breach
- Unit test: disabled -> falls back to binding-window
- Unit test: safe mode -> falls back to binding-window

### Acceptance Criteria
- Correctly weights window scarcity by remaining time and capacity
- Default behavior (threshold=0) matches existing binding-window logic
- Positive threshold enables intelligent cross-window optimization
- Disabled by config or safe mode falls back to conservative approach

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 fleet EMA (docs-5bu) — needs per-window burn rates
- Depends on: P4 target computation (docs-9uz) — replaces binding-window ceiling

## Binding Window Selection and Safe Worker Count

### What to Implement
- `pub fn find_binding_window(forecasts: &mut [WindowRecord])`:

  - Compute and set `safe_w` only on the binding window
- `pub fn compute_safe_workers(remaining_pct: f64, hrs_left: f64, p75_rate_per_worker: f64) -> u32`:

title: P7: System health diagnostic (cgov doctor)
description:
## Task: System Health Diagnostic (cgov doctor)

Validate the entire governor stack in one command with specific remediation steps.

### What to Implement
- New `src/doctor.rs` module:
  - 12 health checks, each returning Pass/Warn/Fail:
    1. OAuth credentials: valid, >1h? <30min? Expired/missing?
    2. API reachability: 200 OK <2s? Slow? Unreachable?
    3. Token collector: running, cursors advancing? Stale >10min? Not running?
    4. Burn rate samples: >=5 per window? 3-4? <3?
    5. Pricing config: all detected models have entries? Unknown model?
    6. Model generation: rates match known generation? Opus at legacy rates?
    7. Promotion dates: active/future? Expires <48h? Expired in config?
    8. SQLite integrity: PRAGMA integrity_check passes?
    9. JSONL/DB sync: row counts within 1%? Diverge? DB missing?
    10. Daemon status: running, last cycle <2x interval? >2x? Not running?
    11. Log file: exists, <100MB? >100MB? Missing?
    12. Prediction accuracy: median error <5%? 5-10%? >10%?
  - Each check has a specific remediation command on failure
  - `cgov doctor` subcommand:
    - Human output: checkmark/warning/cross table
    - `--json`: structured pass/warn/fail per check
  - Exit codes: 0 = all pass (warnings OK), 1 = any fail

### Files

description:
## Incremental JSONL Reader with Shrinkage Guard

Implement the incremental line reader that seeks to a byte offset and reads new lines, with shrinkage detection for log-rotated files.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add incremental reader function

### What to Implement
- `pub fn read_new_lines(path: &Path, cursor: &mut CursorStore) -> Result<Vec<String>>`:
  - Get stored offset via cursor.get_offset(path)
  - Check current file size: if file size < stored offset, log warning `[collector] cursor reset for {path} (file shrunk: {stored} -> {actual} bytes)` and reset offset to 0
  - Seek to byte offset, read all bytes to EOF
  - Split into lines, filter out empty lines
  - Update cursor with new byte offset (end of file)
  - Return the new lines as Vec<String>

### Test Command
```bash
cargo test --lib collector::tests::read_new 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: write 3 lines to temp file, read_new_lines with offset 0 returns all 3 lines
- Unit test: incremental read — write 2 lines, read (get 2), write 2 more, read again (get only new 2), verify cursor offset updated
- Unit test: shrinkage guard — write 100 bytes, set cursor offset to 100, truncate file to 10 bytes, read_new_lines resets offset to 0 and returns all content
- Unit test: empty file returns empty Vec
- Unit test: file with trailing newline doesn't produce empty trailing line
- Shrinkage guard must log the warning message (capture log output or use tracing test subscriber)

description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: /home/coding/claude-governor/docs/plan/plan.md

## Overview
Claude Governor (cgov) is a quota-aware capacity governor that monitors Claude Code subscription usage in real time, predicts per-window exhaustion, and scales worker fleets to prevent premature cutoff. Ships as a single statically-linked Rust binary with zero runtime dependencies.

## Progress
- [x] Phase 1: Usage Poller — Direct API polling via ureq+rustls, token refresh, error escalation
- [x] Phase 1b: Token Collector — Independent daemon tailing Claude Code JSONL, i/f/w record types, SQLite mirror
- [x] Phase 2: Schedule & Promotion — Peak/off-peak calculator, promotions.json, promotion validation
- [x] Phase 3: Adaptive Burn Rate — Per-model EMA, per-window capacity forecast, p75 variance-aware planning
- [x] Phase 4: Core Governor Loop — Main daemon, worker manager (launch_cmd/heartbeat), hysteresis, emergency brake
- [x] Phase 5: Alert Manager — HUMAN-type beads, cooldown dedup, underutilization sprint trigger
- [ ] Phase 6: Integration & CLI — Wire poller+collector+burn_rate into daemon loop, agent config, full status display, init/enable/disable/start/stop, explain, doctor
- [ ] Phase 7b: Advanced Features — Pre-scaling, cross-window optimization, cache efficiency, confidence cone, safe mode wiring
- [ ] Phase 8: Deployment — Release binary, install to ~/.local/bin/cgov

## Verification
- 328 lib tests + 3 binary tests pass
- cargo build succeeds
- Individual modules (poller, collector, burn_rate, governor, etc.) are functionally complete
- Integration between modules in the daemon loop is the primary remaining work

title: Add sustained low cache efficiency alert with configurable threshold and window
description:
## Goal
Fire an alert when the fleet's cache-read-to-total-token ratio stays below a configurable threshold for N consecutive polling intervals. This detects workloads that are not benefiting from prompt caching.

## Why
Low cache efficiency means workers are burning more tokens per task than expected. This affects burn rate accuracy and cost. A sustained drop (not just a single spike) indicates a structural issue worth surfacing.

## Implementation
- In alerts.rs: add LowCacheEfficiency alert variant (already has stub per recent commits)
- Track cache_efficiency_ratio per interval in governor state: cache_reads / total_tokens
- If ratio < config.alerts.low_cache_efficiency_threshold (default: 0.3) for >= N consecutive intervals (default: 3): fire alert
- Alert body: current ratio, threshold, consecutive intervals below threshold
- Respect existing per-alert-type cooldown mechanism
- Expose cache_efficiency_ratio in cgov status output
- Add unit tests for threshold boundary, cooldown, recovery

## Config additions (governor.yaml)
alerts:
  low_cache_efficiency_threshold: 0.3
  low_cache_efficiency_consecutive_intervals: 3

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] cache_efficiency_ratio tracked per poll interval
- [ ] Alert fires when ratio sustained below threshold
- [ ] Cooldown respected (no spam)
- [ ] Ratio visible in cgov status --json
- [ ] Unit tests for boundary conditions

description:
## Task: Main Governor Daemon Loop

Implement the core daemon loop that ties together all components into a continuous governor cycle.

### What to Implement
- In `src/governor.rs`:
  - `run_daemon(config: &Config)`: Main loop:
    1. `usage = poll_usage()` — call the poller
    2. `schedule = compute_schedule()` — peak/off-peak, effective hours
    3. `burn_rate = compute_burn_rate()` — read from collector DB, update EMA
    4. `target = compute_target_workers(usage, schedule, burn_rate)` — per-agent targets
    5. `current = count_workers()` — heartbeat + tmux verification
    6. `apply_scaling(current, target)` — scale up/down with hysteresis
    7. `check_alerts(usage, schedule)` — alert conditions
    8. `write_state()` — atomic state file update
    9. `sleep(LOOP_INTERVAL)` — configurable, default 300s
  - Signal handling: SIGINT/SIGTERM -> graceful shutdown (finish current cycle, exit)
  - Error handling: never crash — log errors, continue to next cycle
  - Logging: structured per-cycle summary with window status, worker counts, actions taken
  - `--dry-run` mode: compute and log everything but skip apply_scaling()

### Files
- `src/governor.rs` (extend)
- `src/main.rs` (add `cgov daemon` and `cgov daemon --dry-run` subcommands)

### Testing Requirements
- Integration test: mock all components, verify correct call sequence
- Unit test: error in one component doesn't crash daemon (logs and continues)
- Unit test: dry-run mode logs target but doesn't scale
- Unit test: signal handling triggers clean exit
- Unit test: state file updated after each cycle

### Acceptance Criteria
- Daemon runs continuously until interrupted
- Never crashes on component errors
- dry-run mode fully functional
- Structured logging per cycle
- State file atomically updated each cycle
- Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P4 worker manager (docs-x8d) — needs scale_up/scale_down
- Depends on: P4 target computation (docs-9uz) — needs compute_target_workers

title: P3: Fleet-level EMA and capacity forecast
description:
## Task: Fleet-Level EMA and Capacity Forecast

Aggregate instance burn rates into fleet statistics and maintain per-(model, window) EMA for capacity forecasting.

### What to Implement
- In `src/burn_rate.rs`:
  - `FleetBurnStats` struct: mean, p75, stddev of per-worker rates
  - `aggregate_fleet_burn(instances: &[InstanceBurnRate]) -> FleetBurnStats`:
    - Compute mean, p75, stddev across all active sessions
    - p75 is the conservative rate used for capacity planning
  - `EmaState` struct: per-(model, window) EMA value, sample count
  - `update_ema(state: &mut EmaState, new_value: f64, alpha: f64)`:
    - `ema = alpha * new_value + (1 - alpha) * prev_ema`
    - alpha defaults to 0.2 from config
  - `CapacityForecast` struct per window:
    - `target_ceiling`, `current_utilization`, `remaining_pct` (ceil - used)
    - `hours_remaining`, `fleet_pct_per_hour`
    - `predicted_exhaustion_hours` = remaining_pct / fleet_pct_per_hour
    - `cutoff_risk` = exh_hrs < hrs_left
    - `margin_hrs` = hrs_left - exh_hrs
    - `binding` flag, `safe_worker_count`
  - `compute_capacity_forecast(usage, ema_states, workers, config) -> HashMap<String, CapacityForecast>`
  - `find_binding_window(forecasts) -> String`: argmin(margin_hrs)
  - `compute_safe_workers(remaining_pct, hrs_left, p75_rate) -> u32`: floor(remaining / hrs_left / p75)
  - Separate peak/off-peak tokens_per_pct storage for promotion validation
  - Baseline fallback: use baseline_burn_rate from config until 3 valid samples per window
  - Discard samples > 3σ from current EMA per window

### Files
- `src/burn_rate.rs` (extend)
- `src/state.rs` (extend — write burn_rate and capacity_forecast to state file)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: EMA converges to steady-state value after N samples
- Unit test: fleet aggregate p75 and stddev with 3 synthetic instances
- Unit test: capacity forecast — known inputs produce correct exh_hrs, cutoff_risk, margin_hrs
- Unit test: safe_worker_count computation with floor behavior
- Unit test: binding window is the one with smallest margin_hrs
- Unit test: baseline fallback used when < 3 samples per window
- Unit test: outlier rejection (3σ from EMA)
- Unit test: each window independently transitions from baseline to EMA

### Acceptance Criteria
- Per-(model, window) EMA maintains state across cycles
- Capacity forecast computed for all 3 windows
- Binding window correctly identified
- Conservative p75 used for safe_worker_count
- Baseline fallback per-window (not global)
- Outliers rejected without corrupting EMA

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 per-instance burn rate (docs-1e4)
- Depends on: P2 schedule calculator (docs-6dm) — needs peak/off-peak classification

comments.author: coding
comments.text:
Wrote a zero-usage heartbeat fleet record in run_collection_pass() when session_usage is empty (no new data). Previously the early return skipped the database write, letting the governor's freshness check see a stale t1 timestamp and fire false collector_offline alerts during idle periods.

## Retrospective
- **What worked:** Reading the systemd journal to pinpoint the exact 6-minute gap (10:03:49–10:09:49) where three consecutive 'no new usage data' passes left the fleet aggregate stale, confirming the diagnosis without guessing.
- **What didn't:** Nothing failed — the fix was straightforward once the idle-period gap was confirmed in the logs.
- **Surprise:** The standalone collector service and the governor's embedded collector both run run_collection_pass() independently, so the same idle gap appears in both service logs. The fix covers both paths since they share the same function.
- **Reusable pattern:** When a daemon has a liveness freshness check downstream, any early-return code path that skips the normal heartbeat write will cause false offline alerts. Always write a heartbeat record on every successful pass, even if there is nothing substantive to report.

description:
## Task: Peak/Off-Peak Schedule Calculator

Implement core schedule awareness functions in src/schedule.rs.

### What to Implement
- New `src/schedule.rs` module:
  - `is_peak_now() -> bool`: Peak = 08:00-14:00 ET weekdays (half-open: 08:00 is peak, 14:00 is off-peak)
  - `is_peak_at(t: DateTime<Utc>) -> bool`: Same logic for arbitrary timestamp
  - `is_weekend(t: DateTime<Utc>) -> bool`: Saturday/Sunday always off-peak
  - `current_multiplier(promotions: &[Promotion]) -> f64`: Returns active promotion multiplier or 1.0
  - `get_multiplier_at(t: DateTime<Utc>, promotions: &[Promotion]) -> f64`: Multiplier at arbitrary time
  - `effective_hours_remaining(reset_time: DateTime<Utc>, promotions: &[Promotion]) -> f64`:
    - Walk forward from now to reset_time in 1-minute steps
    - Apply multiplier at each step
    - Return sum (effective hours accounting for 2x off-peak)
  - `Promotion` struct: name, start date, end date, peak_start_hour_et, peak_end_hour_et, offpeak_multiplier, applies_to windows
  - `load_promotions(path: &Path) -> Vec<Promotion>`: Load from promotions.json

### Files
- `src/schedule.rs` (new module)
- `config/promotions.json` (create with March 2026 promotion entry)
- `src/main.rs` (add `mod schedule`)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: 7:59 AM ET weekday -> off-peak (multiplier 1.0 with no promo, or promo multiplier during promo)
- Unit test: 8:00 AM ET weekday -> peak (multiplier 1.0)
- Unit test: 2:00 PM ET weekday -> off-peak
- Unit test: Saturday 10:00 AM -> off-peak (always)
- Unit test: past promo end date -> multiplier 1.0
- Unit test: effective_hours_remaining with 40h reset including 30h off-peak should be > 40
- Unit test: effective_hours_remaining with no promo -> equals raw hours

### Acceptance Criteria
- Correct ET timezone handling (handles DST)
- Half-open interval: 08:00 inclusive start, 14:00 exclusive end
- Weekend always off-peak regardless of promo
- effective_hours_remaining accounts for mixed peak/off-peak segments
- promotions.json loaded correctly with serde

### Dependencies
- None (standalone module)

description:
## InstanceRecord Struct, Serialization, and Peak Detection

Implement the InstanceRecord struct and time-based helpers for peak/off-peak detection.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add InstanceRecord struct and time helpers

### What to Implement
- `pub struct InstanceRecord` with all wide-schema fields:
  - `r: String` (always "i"), `ts: DateTime<Utc>`, `t0: DateTime<Utc>`, `t1: DateTime<Utc>`
  - `sess: String`, `sid: String`, `model: String`
  - `pk: bool` (peak flag), `hr_et: u8`, `dow: u8` (day of week 0=Mon)
  - Token columns: `input_n: u64`, `input_usd: f64`, `output_n: u64`, `output_usd: f64`, `r_cache_n: u64`, `r_cache_usd: f64`, `w_cache_n: u64`, `w_cache_usd: f64`, `w_cache_1h_n: u64`, `w_cache_1h_usd: f64`, `total_usd: f64`
  - Window pct fields: `p5h: Option<f64>`, `p7d: Option<f64>`, `p7ds: Option<f64>` (null at write time)
- Implement `Serialize` via serde with `#[serde(rename)]` to match exact JSONL field names (e.g., `input-n`, `r-cache-usd`)
- `pub fn is_peak(t: DateTime<Utc>) -> bool` — peak = 8AM-2PM ET weekdays (convert UTC to US/Eastern)
- `pub fn compute_hr_et(t: DateTime<Utc>) -> u8` — hour in Eastern time
- `pub fn compute_dow(t: DateTime<Utc>) -> u8` — day of week in Eastern time (0=Monday)

### Test Command
```bash
cargo test --lib collector::tests::instance 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: InstanceRecord serializes to JSON with correct field names (input-n, r-cache-usd, etc.)
- Unit test: is_peak returns true for weekday 10am ET (UTC 14:00 or 15:00 depending on DST)
- Unit test: is_peak returns false for weekday 3pm ET
- Unit test: is_peak returns false for weekend 10am ET
- Unit test: compute_dow returns 0 for Monday
- Unit test: window pct fields serialize as null when None

title: P4: Emergency brake (98% hard stop)
description:
## Task: Emergency Brake (98% Hard Stop)

Implement the hard emergency brake that scales all workers to 0 when any window hits 98%.

### What to Implement
- In `src/governor.rs`:
  - `check_emergency_brake(usage: &UsageSnapshot) -> Option<EmergencyBrake>`:
    - Check all windows: if any utilization >= 98%, trigger brake
    - `EmergencyBrake` struct: triggered_window, utilization_pct
  - When triggered:
    - Scale ALL agents to 0 workers immediately (override hysteresis, override idle-only rule)
    - Log `EMERGENCY BRAKE APPLIED — {win} at {pct}%`
    - Set state flag: `emergency_brake_active = true`
    - Create HUMAN alert bead
  - Brake fires on observed utilization, NOT forecasts (independent of cutoff_risk)
  - Brake persists until utilization drops below 98% or window resets

### Files
- `src/governor.rs` (extend)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: 97.9% -> no brake
- Unit test: 98.0% -> brake triggers
- Unit test: brake scales ALL agents to 0
- Unit test: brake overrides hysteresis band
- Unit test: brake clears when utilization drops below 98%
- Unit test: brake clears when window resets

### Acceptance Criteria
- Hard stop at 98% regardless of other calculations
- All agents scaled to 0 (not just one)
- Overrides hysteresis — immediate action
- Clear logging and alert creation
- Automatic recovery when condition clears

### Dependencies

title: [CRITICAL] emergency_brake_activated: Emergency brake active since 2026-04-23T01:21:03.309820710+00:00
[WARNING] sonnet_cutoff_risk: Seven-day Sonnet window at cutoff risk: 15.0% utilized, 145.2h remaining, margin_hrs=-140.6h
Alert thresholding produces 100% false positives; stop auto-creating beads for unvalidated alerts
description:
## Problem

As of 2026-04-23, every single one of the 50 most recently closed beads in claude-governor is a `docs-*` bead that was auto-created from an alert (`sonnet_cutoff_risk`, `cutoff_imminent`, `emergency_brake_activated`, `collector_offline`) and closed with a commit of the form:

```
Document docs-jnvh as emergency_brake_activated false positive (98% util, -17.2h margin)
Document docs-q4sj as sonnet_cutoff_risk false positive (86% util, -16.2h margin)
Document docs-tggx as cutoff_imminent false positive (99% util, -16.2h margin)
```

**FP rate in the observed window: 50/50 = 100%.** This loop produces ~298 commits/7d — about 25% of total repo-wide commit volume — with zero engineering value.

## Fleet impact

- Workers spend ~25% of capacity round-tripping these alerts (alert fires → `docs-*` bead spawns → worker claims → "document as false positive" commit → close).
- When a worker dies mid-alert-handling, the `docs-*` bead becomes an in_progress zombie. 19 of the 53 total in_progress beads on 2026-04-22 were stuck claude-governor alerts with ages 50h–220h.
- Velocity metrics are inflated: real engineering work is ~127 commits/day vs. a reported ~169. The 500 commits/day target is 25% of the way there, not 34%.

## Suspected root cause

The alert bodies report utilization `81%–99%` alongside margins of `-15.2h` to `-23.2h` (negative). A negative margin at sub-100% util is self-contradictory — either the margin math is wrong or the thresholds are inverted. Whichever it is, the predicate that fires these alerts is broken across every alert type uniformly, not just one.

Starting points for investigation:
- Burn-rate / margin calculation that feeds `sonnet_cutoff_risk`, `cutoff_imminent`, `emergency_brake_activated`.
- The `safe_worker_count` fallback logic (separately tracked in recent `docs-yk3r`, `docs-3gh2`, `docs-khar`, `docs-2dy4` beads — all flagged as bugs, none yet fixed).

## Fix in two parts

**(1) Correct the alert predicates** so the FP rate drops below 5% measured across any 100-bead window.

**(2) Interim mitigation: gate the alert→bead pipeline.** Until (1) lands, stop auto-creating beads for these alert classes. Keep the alert logs for diagnosis; don't burn fleet cycles documenting false positives. Concrete options:
  - Feature flag `governor.alerts.auto_bead = false` (fastest).
  - Require N consecutive cycles in alert state before spawning a bead (smooths out momentary spikes).
  - Suppress spawning when margin and utilization are inconsistent (e.g. negative margin at util < 100%).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] FP rate for `sonnet_cutoff_risk`, `cutoff_imminent`, `emergency_brake_activated`, `collector_offline` measured at <5% over a 100-bead rolling window.
- [ ] Beads are no longer auto-spawned for these alert classes until the FP rate target is met (interim mitigation in place within this bead).
- [ ] Telemetry/dashboard exposes alert FP rate so regressions are visible.
- [ ] New test: negative-margin-at-sub-100%-util alert is suppressed at source (consistency check).
- [ ] Existing zombie `docs-*` beads (ages >6h) are closed out as part of landing this fix.

## Related

- `needle-mv9t` (2026-04-22): cross-workspace mend gap — would clean up zombies produced by this loop, but doesn't address the root cause.
- `docs-yk3r`, `docs-3gh2`, `docs-khar`, `docs-2dy4`: previously-identified governor bugs that likely share upstream causes.
close_reason: Alert FP rate fixed: consistency guard suppresses negative-margin-at-sub-100%-util (hard_limit_remaining_pct > 5%), auto_bead disabled in config, EmergencyBrakeActivated bead creation disabled, AlertFpTelemetry added to governor-state.json. Closed 20 zombie docs-* beads. 439/440 tests pass (1 pre-existing unrelated failure in collector).

Wire up the token collector as CLI subcommands and implement the daemon loop.

- `src/collector.rs` (top-level `run_collection_pass()` and `run_daemon()` functions)

- Unit test: daemon loop respects interval timing
- Unit test: signal handling triggers clean shutdown
- Test: `cgov token-history --rebuild-db` produces same data as direct collection

title: P4: Target worker computation with hysteresis
description:
## Task: Target Worker Computation with Hysteresis

Implement compute_target_workers() and the hysteresis band that prevents scaling oscillation.

### What to Implement
- In `src/governor.rs` (new module):
  - `compute_target_workers(usage, schedule, burn_rate, config) -> u32`:
    - Compute target_ceiling per window from target_utilization
    - remaining_capacity = max(0, target_ceiling - current_pct)
    - target_rate_per_effective_hour = remaining_capacity / effective_hours_remaining
    - target_rate_per_raw_hour = target_rate_per_effective_hour * current_multiplier
    - target_workers = floor(target_rate / burn_rate_per_worker_per_hour)
    - Clamp to [min_workers, max_workers] per agent
    - Use safe_worker_count[binding_window] as ceiling
  - `should_scale(current: u32, target: u32, hysteresis_band: u32) -> ScaleAction`:
    - If current < target - band: scale up
    - If current > target + band: scale down
    - Else: no action (within dead band)
  - `ScaleAction` enum: ScaleUp(u32), ScaleDown(u32), NoAction
  - Default hysteresis_band = 1 (only act when deviation >= 2 workers)
  - Multi-agent: aggregate burn across all enabled agents; scale down highest-cost agent first

### Files
- `src/governor.rs` (new module, partial — main loop in separate task)
- `src/main.rs` (add `mod governor`)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: target computation with known inputs matches hand calculation
- Unit test: hysteresis — target=3, current=4, band=1 -> no action
- Unit test: hysteresis — target=3, current=5, band=1 -> scale down 2
- Unit test: clamping to min/max workers
- Unit test: binding window ceiling overrides target
- Unit test: multi-agent scale-down prefers highest-cost agent

### Acceptance Criteria
- Correct formula matching plan specification
- Hysteresis prevents oscillation on small deviations
- Binding window safe_worker_count acts as hard ceiling
- Multi-agent cost-based scale-down ordering
- All edge cases (zero remaining, past-ceiling) handled

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 fleet EMA (docs-5bu) — needs capacity forecast
- Depends on: P2 schedule calculator (docs-6dm) — needs effective hours

title: [CRITICAL] emergency_brake_activated: Emergency brake active since 2026-04-23T01:21:03.309820710+00:00
description:
## False Positive Analysis

**Alert:** emergency_brake_activated (CRITICAL)
**Activated:** 2026-04-23T01:21:03Z
**Bead:** docs-1w6q

### Evidence of false positive

- seven_day window at 100% utilization, margin_hrs=-7.2h, 7.2h remaining
- seven_day_sonnet window at 86% utilization, 7.2h remaining
- Workers at 0 (emergency brake scaled fleet to 0 on activation)
- No active burn — brake itself prevents any token consumption
- Utilization pinned at 100% because with zero workers, no consumption occurs to change the ratio; the window will reset naturally in ~7.2h

### Root cause

Same as prior false positives (docs-3wbo, docs-j5w0, docs-md2q, docs-unw6): the emergency brake triggers at 98% utilization, kills all workers, and then utilization cannot decrease because there's no consumption to shift the ratio. The alert re-fires every 60 minutes (cooldown) until the seven_day window resets.

### Status

False positive — no action required. The window will reset and the brake will clear automatically.

title: P5: Alert condition checker and cooldown dedup
description:
## Task: Alert Condition Checker and Cooldown Dedup

Implement alert condition evaluation with per-type cooldown deduplication.

### What to Implement
- New `src/alerts.rs` module:
  - `AlertType` enum: CutoffImminent, SonnetCutoffRisk, SessionCutoffRisk, BurnRateSpike, Underutilization, TokenRefreshFailing, EmergencyBrakeActivated, PromotionNotApplying, CollectorOffline
  - `AlertCondition` struct: alert_type, message, severity
  - `check_alert_conditions(state: &GovernorState, config: &Config) -> Vec<AlertCondition>`:
    - CutoffImminent: any window cutoff_risk=1 with margin_hrs < -2
    - SonnetCutoffRisk: seven_day_sonnet.cutoff_risk=1
    - SessionCutoffRisk: five_hour.cutoff_risk=1
    - BurnRateSpike: burn_rate_sample > baseline * 2
    - Underutilization: all windows margin_hrs > hrs_left * 0.5
  - `AlertCooldown` struct: per-type `last_fired` timestamps in state
  - `should_fire(alert_type, last_fired, cooldown_minutes) -> bool`:
    - Suppress if same type fired within cooldown_minutes (default 60)
    - Allow if condition cleared and re-triggered after cooldown
  - `update_cooldown(state: &mut GovernorState, alert_type, now)`

### Files
- `src/alerts.rs` (new module)
- `src/main.rs` (add `mod alerts`)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: each alert condition triggers correctly from synthetic state
- Unit test: cooldown suppresses duplicate within window
- Unit test: cooldown allows re-fire after expiry
- Unit test: cooldown allows re-fire after condition cleared and re-triggered
- Unit test: multiple simultaneous alert conditions

### Acceptance Criteria
- All alert types from plan implemented
- Per-type cooldown prevents spam
- Cooldown timestamps persisted in state file
- Alert messages contain specific window names, percentages, and hours

title: Empirically validate 2x off-peak promotion from observed token consumption ratios
description:
## Goal
Validate the 2x off-peak promotion multiplier by comparing observed peak vs off-peak token-per-percent ratios from token-history data. Fall back to 1x if empirical ratio is not within 10% of declared 2.0.

## Why
The promotion schedule is calendar-based (hardcoded March 2026 dates). If the promotion window shifts, expires, or was misconfigured, the governor would over-estimate capacity during off-peak and under-estimate during peak — leading to cutoffs.

## Implementation
- In collector.rs or burn_rate.rs: group token records by peak/off-peak periods using schedule.rs
- Compute avg tokens-per-percent-usage during each period type
- If off_peak_rate / peak_rate is within [1.8, 2.2], accept promotion as active (ratio ~2.0)
- If ratio < 1.8 or data insufficient: fall back to 1x multiplier (conservative)
- If ratio > 2.5: log anomaly alert (possible miscalibration)
- Expose observed_promo_ratio in governor state and cgov status output
- Add test cases for ratio boundary conditions

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Observed promo ratio computed from token-history DB
- [ ] Scheduler uses empirical ratio when sufficient data exists (>= 10 samples each period)
- [ ] Falls back to 1x when data insufficient or ratio out of range
- [ ] observed_promo_ratio surfaced in cgov status --json
- [ ] Alert fired when ratio anomaly detected (> 2.5 or < 0.8)

title: Composite risk optimization: weight binding window by duration, volatility, and margin
description:
## Goal
Replace the current binding window selection (based solely on margin_hrs) with a composite risk score that weights each window by:
- **Margin** (hours remaining before exhaustion)
- **Duration** (5h window is higher risk than 7d window at same margin%)
- **Volatility** (p25/p50/p75 cone spread — wide cone = uncertain forecast = higher risk)
- **Time-to-reset** (how soon can we recover if we exhaust?)

## Why
The current approach picks the window with the smallest margin_hrs absolute. But a 5-hour window with 1hr margin is far more dangerous than a 7-day window with 6hr margin. Duration and volatility should amplify the risk score.

## Proposed Formula
risk_score = (1.0 - margin_pct) * duration_weight * volatility_factor
- duration_weight: 5h → 3.0, 7d → 1.0, 7d-sonnet → 1.5
- volatility_factor: cone_ratio (p75 - p25) / p50 — wider = higher risk

## Implementation
- Add risk_score computation in burn_rate.rs per-window
- Update binding window selection in governor.rs to use max risk_score
- Surface risk_score in state.rs and status_display.rs
- Add unit tests for composite risk edge cases

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] risk_score computed for each window
- [ ] Binding window selected by max risk_score (not min margin_hrs)
- [ ] risk_score visible in cgov status --json
- [ ] Unit tests pass

title: JSONL file discovery and cursor store
description:
## JSONL File Discovery and Cursor Store

Implement file discovery via glob and the persistent cursor store for incremental reading.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add functions (module already exists with UsageRecord etc.)
- `Cargo.toml` — add `glob` crate dependency if not present

### What to Implement
- `pub fn discover_jsonl_files(base: &Path) -> Vec<PathBuf>` — walks `base/**/*.jsonl` using glob, returns sorted list of paths
- `pub struct CursorStore { cursors: HashMap<PathBuf, u64> }` with:
  - `pub fn load(path: &Path) -> Result<Self>` — loads `~/.needle/state/collector-cursors.json`, returns empty map if file missing
  - `pub fn save(&self, path: &Path) -> Result<()>` — atomic write: serialize to JSON, write to .tmp file, rename to final path
  - `pub fn get_offset(&self, file: &Path) -> u64` — returns stored offset or 0 for unknown files
  - `pub fn set_offset(&mut self, file: &Path, offset: u64)` — updates offset for file

### Test Command
```bash
cargo test --lib collector::tests::cursor 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: CursorStore round-trip — save to temp file, load back, verify all offsets match
- Unit test: load from nonexistent path returns empty CursorStore (no error)
- Unit test: get_offset for unknown file returns 0
- Unit test: discover_jsonl_files finds .jsonl files in nested directories (create temp dir structure)
- Unit test: discover_jsonl_files ignores non-.jsonl files
- Atomic write: save() writes to .tmp then renames (verify by checking no .tmp file remains)

title: Phase 1b: Token Collector daemon
description:
## Phase 1b: Token Collector (Independent Data Capture)

Build the token collector daemon that tails Claude Code JSONL session files and captures model-specific, token-type-specific consumption data.

### Deliverables
- src/collector.rs module:
  - Walk ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl for unprocessed lines
  - Parse assistant message usage blocks (input, output, cache_read, cache_creation with ephemeral_5m and ephemeral_1h tiers)
  - Extract model from message or infer from session path
  - Accumulate deltas per model per collection interval
  - Compute dollar equivalent using pricing from governor.yaml config
  - Append JSONL records to ~/.needle/state/token-history.jsonl (3 record types: i=instance, f=fleet, w=window)
  - Mirror to token-history.db SQLite for fast queries

- Cursor tracking (collector-cursors.json):
  - Store {filepath: byte_offset} for incremental scanning
  - Shrinkage guard: detect truncated files, reset cursor to 0

- SQLite mirror with tables: i, f, w (wide schemas matching JSONL record types)
  - Views: instance_compare, promo_check

- cgov collect CLI subcommand (standalone, no daemon required)
- cgov collect --daemon mode (continuous loop)
- cgov token-history query subcommands (--last, --compare, --fleet, --rebuild-db)

### Tests
- Dollar computation against known API pricing (each tok_type x model)
- Delta verification (second pass emits zero-n records)
- Multi-model attribution
- Fleet variance stats with synthetic data
- Window binding selection (5h vs 7d constraint)

P7: Forecast confidence cone
description:
## Task: Forecast Confidence Cone

Replace single-point exhaustion predictions with range estimates using per-worker variance.

### What to Implement
- In `src/burn_rate.rs` (extend):
  - Compute per-window exhaustion prediction cone:
    - rate_p25 = ema_rate - 0.675 * stddev (optimistic, 25th percentile)
    - rate_p50 = ema_rate (expected)
    - rate_p75 = ema_rate + 0.675 * stddev (conservative, 75th percentile)
    - exh_hrs_p25 = remaining_pct / (rate_p25 * workers) — best case
    - exh_hrs_p50 = remaining_pct / (rate_p50 * workers) — expected
    - exh_hrs_p75 = remaining_pct / (rate_p75 * workers) — worst case
  - `cone_ratio = exh_hrs_p25 / exh_hrs_p75` (or p75/p25 of rates)
  - Decision logic modulation:
    - Narrow cone (ratio < 1.5): act on p50 (confident)
    - Wide cone (ratio > 2.0): act on p75 (conservative)
    - Between: linear blend between p50 and p75
  - Extend `w` record fields: `exh_hrs_p25`, `exh_hrs_p50`, `exh_hrs_p75`, `cone_ratio`
  - Extend `cgov status` output: `CUTOFF 2.0-3.8h` range instead of single value
  - Extend `cgov simulate` to output three trajectory lines (best/expected/worst)
  - Safe mode interaction: always use p75 regardless of cone width

### Files
- `src/burn_rate.rs` (extend)
- `src/collector.rs` (extend w record)
- `src/cli.rs` (extend status display)
- `src/simulator.rs` (extend with cone)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: cone computation with known stddev
- Unit test: narrow cone -> act on p50
- Unit test: wide cone -> act on p75
- Unit test: linear blend in between
- Unit test: safe mode always uses p75
- Unit test: w record contains cone fields

### Acceptance Criteria
- Three-point prediction per window (p25/p50/p75)
- Decision automatically more conservative when variance high
- Status display shows range instead of point estimate
- Safe mode overrides to always-p75
- cone_ratio drives scaling aggressiveness

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 fleet EMA (docs-5bu) — needs stddev data
- Depends on: P7 safe mode (docs-ux4) — interacts with safe mode
