description:
## Task: Daemon Management — systemd and tmux Modes

Implement cgov start/stop/restart/enable/disable with dual-mode daemon management.

### What to Implement
- In `src/daemon.rs` (new module):
  - Mode detection: check for systemd user session availability
  - **Mode A: systemd user service** (Linux default):
    - `cgov enable`: install unit files, daemon-reload, enable + start both services
    - `cgov disable`: stop + disable both services
    - `cgov start`: start services (must be enabled first)
    - `cgov stop`: graceful stop (governor finishes current cycle)
    - `cgov restart`: stop + start
    - Unit files: claude-governor.service and claude-token-collector.service
  - **Mode B: tmux sessions** (fallback):
    - `cgov start`: `tmux new-session -d -s "claude-governor" "cgov _daemon"` (and token-collector)
    - `cgov stop`: send SIGTERM to tmux session processes
  - `_daemon` internal subcommand: the actual daemon entrypoint (used by both modes)
  - `_token-collector` internal subcommand: token collector entrypoint
  - Store chosen mode in governor.yaml as `daemon_mode: systemd|tmux`
  - `cgov logs --follow` works with both modes (tails log file directly)

### Files
- `src/daemon.rs` (new module)
- `systemd/claude-governor.service` (template)
- `systemd/claude-token-collector.service` (template)
- `src/main.rs` (add daemon subcommands)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: systemd detection logic
- Unit test: service file installation to correct path (~/.config/systemd/user/)
- Unit test: tmux fallback creates correct sessions
- Unit test: stop waits for current cycle completion

### Acceptance Criteria
- Auto-detects systemd vs tmux
- Services survive reboot when enabled via systemd
- tmux fallback works on systems without systemd
- Graceful stop ensures no mid-cycle interruption
- Logs accessible regardless of daemon mode

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P4 main daemon loop (docs-4f7) — needs _daemon entrypoint

title: Agent config matches all workers — would scale down other projects
description: The agent config has two problems that would cause incorrect scaling in live mode. (A) launch_cmd hardcodes --workspace /home/coding/claude-governor — the governor should be workspace-agnostic or configurable per deployment. (B) session_pattern 'needle-claude-*' and heartbeat_dir '~/.needle/state/heartbeats' match ALL needle workers across all workspaces, so count_workers sees 16+ heartbeats when only 2 belong to this agent. The governor would try to scale down workers from other projects. Fix: use a dedicated session prefix per governed agent (e.g. 'needle-cgov-') and filter heartbeat files by session prefix. DO NOT split this bead.

title: P6: cgov status — human and JSON output with exit codes
description:
## Task: cgov status — Human and JSON Output with Exit Codes

Implement the primary status display subcommand with dual-mode output.

### What to Implement
- In `src/main.rs` / `src/cli.rs`:
  - `cgov status` subcommand:
    - Read governor-state.json
    - TTY output: colorized table with window status, workers, burn rate, peak status
    - Non-TTY output: raw JSON (full governor-state.json)
    - `--json` flag: force JSON output even on TTY
    - `--watch` flag: clear terminal, re-render every 30s
  - Exit codes:
    - 0 = all windows safe
    - 1 = general error (daemon not running, parse failure)
    - 2 = cutoff risk active (one or more windows)
    - 3 = emergency brake engaged
  - Color coding: green=OK, yellow=approaching ceiling, red=cutoff risk
  - NO_COLOR env var support + non-TTY detection
  - Auto-detect: non-TTY without --json -> emit JSON automatically

### Files
- `src/cli.rs` (new module for CLI output formatting)
- `src/main.rs` (extend with subcommand)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: human output formatting matches plan example
- Unit test: JSON output is valid JSON matching state schema
- Unit test: exit code 0 when all windows safe
- Unit test: exit code 2 when cutoff_risk active
- Unit test: exit code 3 when emergency brake active
- Unit test: NO_COLOR disables color codes

### Acceptance Criteria
- Human output matches plan format exactly
- JSON output is complete governor-state.json
- Exit codes enable branching without JSON parsing
- Color disabled when appropriate (NO_COLOR, non-TTY)
- --watch mode refreshes cleanly

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 state store (docs-thy) — needs state file to read

title: P1b: Instance record (i) and fleet record (f) JSONL writer
description:
## Task: Instance (i) and Fleet (f) JSONL Record Writer

Implement the JSONL record generation for instance-level and fleet-level token consumption data.

### What to Implement
- In `src/collector.rs`:
  - `InstanceRecord` struct matching the wide `i` record schema:
    - `r: "i"`, `ts`, `t0`, `t1`, `sess`, `sid`, `model`, `pk` (peak flag), `hr_et`, `dow`
    - Token columns: `input-n`, `input-usd`, `output-n`, `output-usd`, `r-cache-n`, `r-cache-usd`, `w-cache-n`, `w-cache-usd`, `w-cache-1h-n`, `w-cache-1h-usd`, `total-usd`
    - Window pct fields: `p5h`, `p7d`, `p7ds` (null at write time, annotated later by governor)
  - `FleetRecord` struct matching the wide `f` record schema:
    - `r: "f"`, timestamps, `pk`, `hr_et`, `dow`, `workers`
    - Per-model columns: `{model}-{tok_type}-n`, `{model}-{tok_type}-usd` for all configured models
    - Fleet totals: `total-usd`, `p75-usd-hr`, `std-usd-hr`
    - Window snapshots: `p5h`, `p7d`, `p7ds`, `usd-per-pct-7ds`
  - `aggregate_to_fleet(instances: &[InstanceRecord]) -> FleetRecord`: Sum instance records, compute per-worker stats (mean, p75, stddev)
  - `append_jsonl(path: &Path, records: &[serde_json::Value])`: Atomic append to JSONL file
  - Peak/off-peak detection: `is_peak(t: DateTime) -> bool` — peak = 8AM-2PM ET weekdays
  - `hr_et` and `dow` computation from timestamp

### Files
- `src/collector.rs`

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: single instance record serializes correctly to expected JSON shape
- Unit test: fleet record aggregation from 2 instances — verify sums and per-worker stats
- Unit test: p75 and stddev computation with 3+ synthetic instances
- Unit test: peak flag correctly set for various times (weekday 10am=peak, weekday 3pm=off-peak, weekend=off-peak)
- Unit test: JSONL append atomicity (no partial writes)
- Unit test: zero-activity models produce zero-filled columns in fleet record

### Acceptance Criteria
- Records match the exact JSONL schema from the plan (field names, types)
- Fleet record includes all configured models even when inactive (zero-filled)
- Per-worker variance stats computed correctly
- JSONL file grows append-only, one JSON object per line

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P1b dollar computation (docs-o6d) — needs DollarBreakdown
- Depends on: P1b usage block parser (docs-s7l) — needs UsageRecord

title: Model attribution and session ID extraction
description:
## Model Attribution and Session ID Extraction

Implement per-message model detection and session ID extraction from file paths.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add model extraction and session ID functions

### What to Implement
- `pub fn extract_model(message_json: &serde_json::Value) -> String`:
  - Primary: read `model` field from the message JSON object
  - Fallback: if `model` field is missing/null, return "unknown"
- `pub fn extract_session_id(jsonl_path: &Path) -> String`:
  - Extract session ID from the JSONL file path (typically the filename stem without extension)
  - Example: `/home/user/.claude/projects/foo/abc123.jsonl` -> `abc123`
- `pub fn infer_model_from_path(jsonl_path: &Path) -> Option<String>`:
  - If the path contains model hints (e.g., directory name contains "sonnet" or "opus"), return the inferred model
  - This is a secondary fallback when message-level model field is absent
- Update `parse_usage_block` to use these functions for model and session fields

### Test Command
```bash
cargo test --lib collector::tests::model 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: extract_model with `{"model": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"}` returns "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
- Unit test: extract_model with no model field returns "unknown"
- Unit test: extract_session_id from typical path returns filename stem
- Unit test: infer_model_from_path returns None for generic paths
- Unit test: multi-model session — two lines with different model fields produce different UsageRecords with correct model each

## Task: Dollar Computation and Pricing Engine

Compute dollar-equivalent costs from token counts using configurable per-model pricing.

### What to Implement

Implement the underutilization detection that triggers a sprint to use capacity before window reset.

- Configurable thresholds from governor.yaml

description:
## Task: Window Forecast Record (w) and Binding Window Logic

Implement window forecast records — the primary output of the measurement pipeline.

### What to Implement
- In `src/collector.rs`:
  - `WindowRecord` struct matching the `w` record schema:
    - `r: "w"`, timestamps, `win` (window name), `pk`
    - `ceil` — target ceiling from config (e.g. 90.0)
    - `snap` — raw platform utilization %
    - `reset` — ISO 8601 reset timestamp
    - `delta` — percentage delta this interval
    - `remain` — `ceil - snap` (headroom to ceiling, NOT to 100%)
    - `hrs_left` — hours until window resets
    - `fleet_pct_hr` — fleet burn rate for this window
    - `exh_hrs` — `remain / fleet_pct_hr`
    - `cutoff_risk` — 1 if `exh_hrs < hrs_left`
    - `margin_hrs` — `hrs_left - exh_hrs`
    - `bind` — 1 if this is the most constrained window
    - `safe_w` — max workers where `exh_hrs >= hrs_left` (only on binding window)
  - `compute_window_forecasts(usage_snapshot, fleet_burn_rates, config) -> Vec<WindowRecord>`: Generate 3 records (five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_sonnet)
  - `find_binding_window(forecasts: &[WindowRecord]) -> &WindowRecord`: Smallest/most negative margin_hrs
  - `compute_safe_workers(remaining_pct, hrs_left, p75_rate_per_worker) -> u32`
  - Write 3 `w` records per collection interval after the `f` record

### Files
- `src/collector.rs`

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: window forecast with known values — verify all computed fields
- Unit test: binding window selection when 5h is more constraining than 7d
- Unit test: binding window selection when 7d_sonnet is binding
- Unit test: safe_worker_count computation — verify floor behavior
- Unit test: cutoff_risk=1 when exh_hrs < hrs_left
- Unit test: cutoff_risk=0 when ample headroom
- Unit test: remain uses ceil not 100% (e.g. ceil=85, snap=36 -> remain=49, not 64)

### Acceptance Criteria
- Three w records per interval (one per window)
- Binding window correctly identified
- safe_w only populated on binding window record
- remain computed against target ceiling, not 100%
- All fields match plan schema exactly

P2: Promotion validation against observed consumption
description:
## Task: Promotion Validation Against Observed Consumption

Validate declared promotion multipliers by comparing peak vs off-peak consumption ratios.

### What to Implement
- In `src/schedule.rs` or `src/burn_rate.rs`:
  - `validate_promotion(db: &Connection, promotion: &Promotion) -> PromotionValidation`
  - `PromotionValidation` struct: `validated: bool`, `observed_ratio: f64`, `expected_ratio: f64`, `peak_samples: usize`, `offpeak_samples: usize`
  - Accumulate >=5 peak-hour samples and >=5 off-peak samples at same worker count
  - Compute `observed_ratio = median(tokens_per_pct_offpeak) / median(tokens_per_pct_peak)`
  - Validation rules:
    - If observed_ratio within 10% of declared multiplier: validated=true
    - If observed_ratio < 1.2: promotion likely not applying, fall back to 1x, log warning
    - If observed_ratio > 2.5: unexpected, log anomaly, use observed ratio
  - Write validation result to state: `burn_rate.promotion_validated`
  - Scheduler reads this flag: if false, use multiplier=1.0 (conservative)
  - Use `promo_check` SQLite view for data source

### Files
- `src/schedule.rs` (extend)
- `src/state.rs` (new or extend — state file read/write for promotion_validated flag)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: valid promotion (ratio 1.9-2.1 for declared 2.0) -> validated=true
- Unit test: invalid promotion (ratio 1.0) -> validated=false, fallback to 1x
- Unit test: anomalous ratio (3.0) -> log anomaly, use observed
- Unit test: insufficient samples (<5 peak or <5 off-peak) -> skip validation, use declared
- Unit test: tolerance boundary (exactly ±10%)

### Acceptance Criteria
- Promotion only trusted after empirical validation with sufficient samples
- Conservative fallback (1x) when validation fails
- Anomalous ratios logged but used (better than declared if significantly different)
- State file updated with validation result
- Guards against premature validation with insufficient data

### Dependencies

title: P7: Prediction accuracy self-calibration
description:
## Task: Prediction Accuracy Self-Calibration

Track prediction accuracy and auto-tune governor parameters based on historical performance.

### What to Implement
- New `src/calibrator.rs` module:
  - `score_prediction(window, predicted_pct, actual_pct) -> PredictionScore`:
    - `prediction_error = actual_final_pct - predicted_final_pct`
    - Negative = conservative, positive = aggressive
    - `correct`: predicted exhaustion matched actual
  - Append scored predictions to `~/.needle/state/prediction-accuracy.jsonl`
  - Hook into window reset events to trigger scoring
  - `CalibrationState`: predictions_scored, median_error per window, auto-tuned params
  - Auto-tuning rules (activated after >= 10 scored predictions per window):
    - Median error < -5 (conservative): increase burn_rate_alpha +0.02, widen hysteresis +0.5
    - Median error > +5 (aggressive): decrease alpha -0.02, tighten hysteresis -0.5
    - Stddev > 10 (unpredictable): lower target_utilization -0.02
  - Clamp ranges: alpha [0.05, 0.5], hysteresis [0, 3], target_util [0.70, 0.98]
  - Write calibration state to governor-state.json
  - Auto-tuning opt-in via `calibration.auto_calibrate: true` in config

### Files
- `src/calibrator.rs` (new module)
- `src/main.rs` (add `mod calibrator`)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: scoring with known prediction/actual pairs
- Unit test: auto-tuning direction — conservative data increases alpha
- Unit test: auto-tuning direction — aggressive data decreases alpha
- Unit test: clamp enforcement at boundaries
- Unit test: no tuning until 10 predictions scored
- Unit test: JSONL append format

### Acceptance Criteria
- Prediction accuracy tracked per window
- Auto-tuning adjusts parameters in correct direction
- Clamps prevent runaway parameter drift
- Opt-in via config (tracking always active, tuning optional)
- JSONL file serves as audit trail

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 fleet EMA (docs-5bu) — needs capacity forecast to score
- Depends on: P3 state store (docs-thy) — writes calibration state

title: P7: Cache efficiency monitoring
description:
## Task: Cache Efficiency Monitoring

Track per-worker and per-workspace cache hit ratios to identify inefficient consumption.

### What to Implement
- In `src/collector.rs` (extend):
  - Compute `cache_eff` per instance interval: `cache_read_tokens / (cache_read_tokens + input_tokens)`
  - When both are zero: cache_eff = null (undefined, excluded from aggregation)
  - Add `cache_eff` field to `i` records
  - Add `fleet_cache_eff` (mean) and `cache_eff_p25` (25th percentile) to `f` records
- In `src/db.rs` (extend):
  - `workspace_cache_eff` view: per-session average, min, sample count over last 24h
- In `src/alerts.rs` (extend):
  - Cache efficiency warning: when worker drops below `cache_efficiency.warn_threshold` (default 0.60)
    for `consecutive_intervals` (default 3) consecutive intervals
  - Log: `[governor] CACHE: {session} efficiency {eff} (fleet avg {fleet_avg})`
- In `src/cli.rs` (extend cgov status):
  - Add cache efficiency to status output: `Burn: $2.15/hr (p75) · Cache: 84% (fleet avg)`

### Files
- `src/collector.rs` (extend i and f record generation)
- `src/db.rs` (extend with view)
- `src/alerts.rs` (extend with cache alert)
- `src/cli.rs` (extend status display)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: cache_eff computation with known token counts
- Unit test: null cache_eff when both zero
- Unit test: fleet_cache_eff aggregation
- Unit test: warning triggers after 3 consecutive low-efficiency intervals
- Unit test: warning does NOT trigger for transient dips (1-2 intervals)
- Unit test: workspace_cache_eff view returns correct aggregation

### Acceptance Criteria
- Per-instance cache efficiency tracked and stored
- Fleet-level aggregation in f records
- Sustained low efficiency generates warning
- Status display includes cache efficiency metric
- Null handling prevents division by zero

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P1b i/f record writer (docs-lfz) — extends record format
- Depends on: P5 alert conditions (docs-e5l) — adds new alert type

title: P7: Safe mode — automatic conservatism on prediction degradation
description:
## Task: Safe Mode — Automatic Conservatism

When prediction accuracy degrades, enter a conservative fallback mode.

### What to Implement
- In `src/governor.rs` (extend):
  - `check_safe_mode(calibration: &CalibrationState, config: &SafeModeConfig) -> SafeModeState`
  - Entry conditions (OR):
    - Median prediction error > enter_median_error (default 10.0%)
    - Prediction error stddev > enter_stddev (default 15.0%)
  - Effects while active:
    - target_utilization reduced by util_reduction (default 0.10) — e.g. 0.90 -> 0.80
    - hysteresis_band widened by hysteresis_boost (default 1)
    - Sprint disabled
    - Cross-window optimization disabled (fall back to binding-window)
    - Always use p75 (worst-case) from confidence cone
  - Exit conditions (ALL must be true):
    - Median error < exit_median_error (default 7.0%)
    - Stddev < exit_stddev (default 12.0%)
    - At least 3 new predictions scored since entry
  - Hysteresis between entry/exit thresholds prevents toggling
  - State: safe_mode.active, entered_at, trigger, median_error_at_entry, predictions_since_entry
  - Status: `Workers: 2 active (target: 2 · safe ceiling: 2) WARNING SAFE MODE`
  - Manual override: `cgov scale N` overrides for one cycle but safe mode reasserts next cycle

### Files
- `src/governor.rs` (extend)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: safe mode entry on high median error
- Unit test: safe mode entry on high stddev
- Unit test: safe mode exit requires all three conditions
- Unit test: predictions_since_entry counts window reset events
- Unit test: safe mode disables sprint
- Unit test: safe mode disables cross-window optimization
- Unit test: safe mode reduces target_utilization
- Unit test: manual override logged but safe mode persists

### Acceptance Criteria
- Automatic entry when accuracy degrades
- Conservative parameter adjustments while active
- Sprint and cross-window disabled in safe mode
- Exit requires sustained accuracy recovery
- State visible in cgov status

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P7 self-calibration (docs-rxl) — needs prediction accuracy data
- Depends on: P7 capacity sprint (docs-zi9) — disables sprint
- Depends on: P7 cross-window optimization (docs-13l) — disables optimization

## Task: Promotion Boundary Pre-Scaling

Anticipate multiplier transitions and begin scaling down before the boundary hits.

### What to Implement
- In `src/schedule.rs` (extend):
  - `next_transition(promotions) -> Option<(DateTime, f64, f64)>`:

  - Pre-scale logic in `src/governor.rs`:
    - If transition within `pre_scale_minutes` (default 30 from config):
      - Compute post-transition target workers using new multiplier
      - If post-transition target < current workers: begin scaling down
      - Scale down at most 1 worker per cycle (gradual)
      - `effective_target = max(post_target, current_workers - 1)`
  - Conservative-only: pre-scale DOWN before losing bonus, never pre-scale UP
  - Logging: `[governor] PRE-SCALE: off-peak→peak in {min}min — scaling {from}→{to} (post-transition safe: {safe})`

### Files
- `src/schedule.rs` (extend with next_transition)

title: P4: Worker manager — scale up, scale down, count
description:
## Task: Worker Manager — Scale Up, Scale Down, Count

Implement worker lifecycle management via tmux and heartbeat files.

### What to Implement
- New `src/worker.rs` module:
  - `scale_up(agent: &AgentConfig, count: usize)`:
    - Execute `agent.launch_cmd` via `sh -c` for each new worker
    - Stagger launches with 1s delay between each
    - launch_cmd returns immediately (tmux session created in background)
  - `scale_down_graceful(agent: &AgentConfig, count: usize)`:
    - Read heartbeat JSON files from `agent.heartbeat_dir` matching `agent.session_pattern`
    - Find idle workers (status == "idle")
    - Skip attached sessions (check `tmux display-message -t SESSION '#{session_attached}'`)
    - Send SIGINT via `tmux send-keys SESSION C-c`; sleep 2s; then `tmux kill-session`
    - Kill most-recently-launched idle workers first
    - Stop after killing `count` workers or exhausting idle pool
  - `count_workers(agent: &AgentConfig) -> WorkerCount`:
    - Read heartbeat files + verify against `tmux list-sessions`
    - `WorkerCount`: active, idle, executing, stale
    - Stale heartbeats (>60s old): verify against tmux; remove if session gone
  - `Heartbeat` struct: session, agent, status (idle/executing/starting), bead_id, workspace, updated_at, launched_at
  - `read_heartbeat(path: &Path) -> Option<Heartbeat>`
  - **Key principle**: never kill an executing worker. Only idle workers.

### Files
- `src/worker.rs` (new module)
- `src/main.rs` (add `mod worker`)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: heartbeat parsing (all status values)
- Unit test: stale heartbeat detection (>60s old)
- Unit test: idle worker selection (skip executing, skip attached)
- Unit test: kill order (most recent first)
- Integration test: scale_up executes launch_cmd correctly
- Unit test: count_workers correctly categorizes by status

### Acceptance Criteria
- Never kills executing workers
- Never kills attached sessions (human watching)
- Graceful shutdown with SIGINT before kill
- Stale heartbeat cleanup with tmux verification
- launch_cmd executed via shell (supports complex commands)

### Dependencies
- None (standalone module, uses configured agent settings)

## Phase 2: Schedule and Promotion Calculator

Implement off-peak awareness and promotion-period handling so the governor can accurately compute effective remaining capacity.

  - is_peak_now() -> bool (peak = 8AM-2PM ET weekdays)
  - current_multiplier() -> f64 (1.0 or 2.0 during active promotion)

  - Reads promotion definitions from promotions.json

- config/promotions.json with current promotion entry

- Promotion validation against measured consumption:
  - Accumulate >=5 peak and >=5 off-peak samples at same worker count
  - Compute observed_ratio = median(tokens_per_pct_offpeak) / median(tokens_per_pct_peak)
  - Validate within 10% of declared multiplier
  - Fall back to 1x if validation fails
  - Write validation result to burn_rate.promotion_validated in state

### Tests

- Weekend classification (always off-peak)

- Effective hours calculation: 40h reset with 30h off-peak should be > 40

description:
## Task: Token Collector Offline Graceful Degradation

Implement three-tier fallback when the token collector is not running or data is stale.

### What to Implement
- In `src/burn_rate.rs`:
  - `collector_data_age(db: &Connection) -> Duration`: Time since most recent record in token-history.db
  - Three-tier fallback logic:
    - < 10 minutes: use normally (collector may be between cycles)
    - 10-30 minutes: use last EMA values; log `[governor] WARN: collector data stale ({age}s)`
    - > 30 minutes: fall back to `baseline_burn_rate` from governor.yaml; create HUMAN alert bead
  - In fallback mode: dollar-equivalent metrics unavailable; continue with pct-based rates only
  - When collector resumes: return to EMA-based rates within one interval

### Files
- `src/burn_rate.rs` (extend)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: fresh data (< 10 min) -> normal operation
- Unit test: stale data (15 min) -> warning logged, last EMA used
- Unit test: very stale data (45 min) -> baseline fallback, alert created
- Unit test: recovery — after stale period, fresh data restores normal operation

### Acceptance Criteria
- Governor never crashes when collector offline
- Graceful degradation through three tiers
- Alert created at 30-minute threshold (once, with cooldown)
- Recovery to EMA-based rates is automatic

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 fleet EMA (docs-5bu) — needs EMA infrastructure

description:
## Task: Worker Capacity Awareness (NEEDLE Integration)

Give workers visibility into fleet capacity state via prompt injection.

### What to Implement
- Capacity summary generation in `src/cli.rs` or `src/governor.rs`:
  - `generate_capacity_summary(state: &GovernorState) -> String`:
    - Binding window, headroom, reset time
    - Capacity pressure level: LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH
    - Behavioral recommendation based on pressure
  - Pressure levels:
    - LOW (margin_hrs > hrs_left * 0.5): no constraints, work normally
    - MEDIUM (margin_hrs > 0 but < hrs_left * 0.5): be efficient, don't compromise quality
    - HIGH (cutoff_risk active): actively conserve — prefer Haiku, skip optional steps
  - `cgov status --json` exit codes enable simple conditionals in worker hooks:
    - Exit 0 = safe, 2 = cutoff_risk, 3 = emergency
  - Document the NEEDLE integration point (prompt injection into CLAUDE.md)
  - Graceful degradation: if cgov not installed, block omitted silently

### Files
- `src/cli.rs` (extend with capacity summary generation)
- Documentation for NEEDLE integration point

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: LOW pressure output with ample headroom
- Unit test: MEDIUM pressure output with moderate headroom
- Unit test: HIGH pressure output with cutoff_risk
- Unit test: summary format is valid markdown
- Unit test: exit code mapping

### Acceptance Criteria
- Three distinct pressure levels with appropriate recommendations
- Markdown format suitable for CLAUDE.md injection
- Exit codes work for script-based checking
- Non-breaking when cgov absent (NEEDLE handles graceful fallback)

### Dependencies

title: P7: End-of-window capacity sprint
description:
## Task: End-of-Window Capacity Sprint

Capture throughput from capacity that would expire unused at window reset.

### What to Implement
- In `src/governor.rs` (extend):
  - `sprint_eligible(window, state, config) -> bool`:
    - Window resets in <= sprint.horizon_minutes (default 90)
    - Remaining headroom > sprint.min_headroom_pct (default 15%)
    - Bead backlog exists (workers have work to do)
    - No other window has cutoff_risk
    - Confidence cone not too wide (cone_ratio <= 2.0)
    - Safe mode NOT active
  - When eligible:
    - Temporarily raise max_workers by sprint.max_workers_boost (default 3)
    - effective_max capped at min(safe_worker_count) across non-sprinting windows
    - Set state: sprint_active, sprint_window, sprint_expires_at
  - Sprint ends when: window resets, headroom < 5%, or safe mode activates
  - Status output: `Workers: 5 active (target: 5 · normal max: 3 · SPRINT on five_hour, resets in 0h42m)`

### Files
- `src/governor.rs` (extend)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: sprint triggers with eligible conditions
- Unit test: sprint blocked when other window has cutoff_risk
- Unit test: sprint blocked when headroom too low
- Unit test: sprint blocked when too far from reset
- Unit test: sprint blocked in safe mode
- Unit test: sprint respects cross-window safe_worker_count cap
- Unit test: sprint ends at window reset

### Acceptance Criteria
- Sprint only when conditions safe
- Cross-window safety enforced
- Temporary max_workers boost, reverts automatically
- Sprint state visible in cgov status
- Guards against all inhibiting conditions (safe mode, confidence cone, cross-window risk)

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P4 main daemon loop (docs-4f7)
- Depends on: P5 alert conditions (docs-e5l) — sprint interacts with alerting

title: FleetRecord aggregation and JSONL append
description:
## FleetRecord Aggregation and JSONL Append

Implement the FleetRecord struct, fleet-level aggregation from instance records, and atomic JSONL append.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add FleetRecord struct, aggregation, and append functions

### What to Implement
- `pub struct FleetRecord` with wide schema:
  - `r: String` (always "f"), timestamps, `pk: bool`, `hr_et: u8`, `dow: u8`, `workers: u32`
  - Per-model columns: HashMap or flattened struct for `{model}-{tok_type}-n` and `{model}-{tok_type}-usd`
  - Fleet totals: `total_usd: f64`, `p75_usd_hr: f64`, `std_usd_hr: f64`
  - Window snapshots: `p5h: Option<f64>`, `p7d: Option<f64>`, `p7ds: Option<f64>`, `usd_per_pct_7ds: Option<f64>`
- `pub fn aggregate_to_fleet(instances: &[InstanceRecord]) -> FleetRecord`:
  - Sum all token counts and USD amounts across instances
  - Compute `workers` as count of unique sessions
  - Compute per-worker stats: mean USD/hr, p75 USD/hr (sort values, pick 75th percentile index), stddev USD/hr
  - Zero-fill model columns for models not seen in this batch
- `pub fn append_jsonl(path: &Path, records: &[serde_json::Value]) -> Result<()>`:
  - Open file in append mode (create if missing)
  - Write each record as a single JSON line followed by newline
  - Flush and sync to ensure durability

### Test Command
```bash
cargo test --lib collector::tests::fleet 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: aggregate 2 InstanceRecords — verify fleet total_usd = sum of instance total_usd
- Unit test: p75 computation with 3+ instances — verify correct 75th percentile selection
- Unit test: stddev computation with known values matches expected result (within f64 epsilon)
- Unit test: zero-activity models produce zero-filled columns
- Unit test: append_jsonl writes valid JSONL (each line is valid JSON, ends with newline)
- Unit test: append_jsonl to existing file appends without overwriting
